nodes.text: Without limiting the circumstances in which a child is under the care, supervision or authority of a person, a person (A) has a child (B) under their care, supervision or authority if A is—
B's parent or step-parent; or
B's teacher; or
B's employer; or
B's youth worker; or
B's sports coach; or
B's counsellor; or
B's health professional; or
a person who has parental responsibility (within the meaning of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005) for B; or

a religious or spiritual guide, or a leader or official (including a lay member) of a church or religious body, however any such guide, leader, official, church or body is described, who provides care, advice or instruction to B or has authority over B; or
an out of home carer (within the meaning given by section 161A of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005) of B; or
a police officer acting in the course of their duty in respect of B; or
employed in, or providing services in, a remand centre, youth residential centre, youth justice centre or prison and is acting in the course of their duty in respect of B.
In this section—

nodes.heading: Objectives of Subdivisions (8A) to (8G)
nodes.text: The objectives of Subdivisions (8A) to (8G) are—
to uphold the fundamental right of every person to make decisions about their sexual behaviour and to choose whether or not to engage in sexual activity;

to promote the principle that consent to an act is not to be assumed—that consent involves ongoing and mutual communication and decision-making between each person involved (that is, each person should seek the consent of each other person in a way and at a time that makes it clear whether they consent);
to protect children and persons with a cognitive impairment or mental illness from sexual exploitation.

nodes.heading: Guiding principles
nodes.text: It is the intention of Parliament that in interpreting and applying Subdivisions (8A) to (8G), courts are to have regard to the fact that—
there is a high incidence of sexual violence within society; and
sexual offences are significantly under-reported; and
a significant number of sexual offences are committed against women, children and other vulnerable persons including persons with a cognitive impairment or mental illness; and
sexual offenders are commonly known to their victims; and
sexual offences often occur in circumstances where there is unlikely to be any physical signs of an offence having occurred.

nodes.heading: Assault with intent to commit a sexual offence

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally applies force to another person (B); and
B does not consent to the application of that force; and
at the time of applying that force A intends that B take part in a sexual act; and
A does not reasonably believe that B would consent to taking part in that sexual act.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 4 imprisonment (15 years maximum).
A may commit an offence against subsection (1) even if B is not aware of the application of force by A.
Whether or not A reasonably believes that B would consent to taking part in a sexual act depends on the circumstances.
See section 36B for the effect of intoxication on the standard to be applied in determining whether a person has a reasonable belief.
A's belief that B would consent to a sexual act is not reasonable if A does not say or do anything to find out whether B would consent to the sexual act.
Subsection (3B) does not apply if—
A has a cognitive impairment or mental illness (other than the effects of intoxication that is self-induced within the meaning of section 36B); and
that cognitive impairment or mental illness is a substantial cause of A not saying or doing anything to find out whether B would consent to the sexual act.

Force for the purposes of subsection (1) may be applied—
directly or indirectly; or
to the body of, or to clothing or equipment worn by, B.
In subsection (1)— application of force includes—
application of heat, light, electric current or any other form of energy; and
application of matter in solid, liquid or gaseous form.

nodes.heading: Threat to commit a sexual offence

history.raw: Note to s. 43 repealed by No. 47/2016 s. 14(3).

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A makes to another person (B) a threat to rape or sexually assault B or a third person (C); and
A intends that B will believe, or believes that B will probably believe, that A will carry out the threat.
Words or conduct may constitute a threat for the purposes of subsection (1) if by those words or that conduct an intention to do any of the following is conveyed—
to sexually penetrate or sexually touch B or C without B or C's consent;
to cause B or C, without B or C's consent, to sexually penetrate or sexually touch—
A; or
C or B (as the case requires); or
themselves; or
another person; or
an animal;
to cause B or C, without B or C's consent, to be sexually penetrated or sexually touched by another person or by an animal.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
For the purposes of this section, a threat may be made by words or conduct and may be explicit or implicit.

history.raw: New s. 44 inserted by No. 47/2016 s. 15.

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A makes a threat to another person (B) that A will cause harm of any kind to B, another person or an animal; and
A intends that B will believe, or believes that B will probably believe, that A will cause that harm; and
as a result of A's threat, B or another person takes part (whether at the time the threat is made or at a later time) in a sexual act with A or another person; and
A intends that, as a result of A's threat, an outcome mentioned in paragraph (c) will occur.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1), a threat may be made by words or conduct and may be explicit or implicit.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(c), a person who takes part in a sexual act with A or another person may or may not be the person to whom A has threatened to cause harm.
See section 35C for the meaning of taking part in a sexual act.

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A makes a false or misleading representation; and
A knows that—
the representation is false or misleading; or
the representation is probably false or misleading; and
as a result of A's representation, another person (B) takes part (whether at the time the representation is made or at a later time) in a sexual act with A or another person; and
A intends that, as a result of A's representation, an outcome mentioned in paragraph (c) will occur.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1), a false or misleading representation may be made by words or conduct (including by omission) and may be explicit or implicit.
See section 35C for the meaning of taking part in a sexual act.

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—

causes B to take an intoxicating substance; or
causes another person (C) to administer an intoxicating substance to B; and
A intends that the intoxicating substance—
will impair B's capacity to give, withhold or withdraw consent to taking part in a sexual act; and
will facilitate B taking part in a sexual act with A or another person.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
In this section—

nodes.heading: intoxicating substance

See section 35C for the meaning of taking part in a sexual act.

nodes.heading: Abduction or detention for a sexual purpose

history.raw: New s. 47 inserted by No. 47/2016 s. 15.

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A—
takes away or detains another person (B); or
causes B to be taken away or detained by another person; and
B does not consent to being taken away or detained; and
A knows that—
B does not consent to being taken away or detained; or
B probably does not consent to being taken away or detained; and
A intends that—
B will take part in a sexual act with A or another person (C) or both; or
A or C will marry B (whether or not B consents to being married).
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
It is immaterial that the law prohibits or would not recognise (for whatever reason) a marriage between A and B or between C and B.
See section 35C for the meaning of taking part in a sexual act.

nodes.heading: Sexual activity directed at another person

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A engages in an activity; and
the activity is sexual; and
another person (B) sees the activity or a part of the activity; and
A knows that B will see, or will probably see, the activity or a part of the activity; and
A—
intends that B will experience fear or distress from seeing the activity or a part of the activity; or
knows that B will experience, or will probably experience, fear or distress from seeing the activity or a part of the activity.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the activity was not sexual is not a defence to this offence—see section 48B.

nodes.heading: Exceptions—medical, hygienic, veterinary, agricultural or scientific purposes

nodes.text: A does not commit an offence against—

section 38(1) or 40(1)—if the sexual penetration or touching (as the case requires) is of a person and is done in the course of a procedure carried out in good faith for medical or hygienic purposes; or

section 39(1) or 41(1)—if the sexual penetration or touching (as the case requires) is of a person and is caused by A to be done in the course of a procedure carried out in good faith for medical or hygienic purposes.

A does not commit an offence against section 39(1) or 41(1)—if the sexual penetration or touching (as the case requires) is of an animal and is caused by A to be done in the course of a procedure being carried out in good faith for veterinary or agricultural purposes or scientific research purposes.
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in sections 38, 39, 40 and 41.

nodes.heading: No defence of mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that touching or activity was not sexual
nodes.text: It is not a defence to a charge that, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence, A was under a mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that—
for an offence against section 40(1) or 41(1)—the touching was not sexual; or
for an offence against section 48(1)— the activity was not sexual.
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in sections 40, 41 and 48.

nodes.heading: Sexual assault of a child under the age of 16

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—
touches another person (B); or
causes or allows B to touch A; or
causes B—
to touch, or to continue to touch, themselves; or
to touch, or to continue to touch, another person (C); or
to be touched, or to continue to be touched, by C; and
B is a child under the age of 16 years; and
the touching is—
sexual; and
contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
The standard sentence for an offence against subsection (1) is 4 years.
Whether or not the touching is contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct depends on the circumstances.
For the purposes of subsection (3)—
the circumstances include—
the purpose of the touching; and
whether A seeks or gets sexual arousal or sexual gratification from the touching;
the circumstances do not include—
whether B consents to the touching; or
whether A believes that B consents to the touching.

nodes.heading: Sexual activity in the presence of a child under the age of 16

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—

the activity is sexual; and

A knows that B is, or probably is, present when A engages in the activity; and
B is a child under the age of 16 years; and
engaging in the activity in the presence of B is contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
The standard sentence for an offence against subsection (1) is 4 years.
Whether or not engaging in the activity in the presence of B is contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct depends on the circumstances.
For the purposes of subsection (3)—
the circumstances include—
the purpose of the activity; and
whether A seeks or gets sexual arousal or sexual gratification from engaging in the activity or from the presence of B;
the circumstances do not include—
whether B consents—
to being present when A engages in the activity; or
to A engaging in the activity; or
whether A believes that B consents—
to being present when A engages in the activity; or
to A engaging in the activity.
For the purposes of subsection (1), when A engages in an activity, B may be present—
in person; or
by means of an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000 that is received by B in real time or close to real time.
It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as B was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that B was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as A was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

A defence applies to this offence—see section 49W.

It is immaterial that B was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as A was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.
An exception applies to this offence—see section 49Y.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 49X, 49Z and 49ZA.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the activity was not sexual or that engaging in the activity in the presence of B was not contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct is not a defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Causing a child under the age of 16 to be present during sexual activity

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
another person (B) engages in an activity; and
the activity is sexual; and
another person (C) is present when B engages in the activity; and
A intentionally causes or allows C to be present when B engages in the activity; and
C is a child under the age of 16 years; and
A's causing or allowing C to be present when B engages in the activity is contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
The standard sentence for an offence against subsection (1) is 4 years.
Whether or not causing or allowing C to be present when B engages in the activity is contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct depends on the circumstances.
For the purposes of subsection (3)—
the circumstances include—
the purpose of the activity; and
whether A seeks or gets sexual arousal or sexual gratification from B engaging in the activity or from the presence of C;
the circumstances do not include—
whether C consents—
to being present when B engages in the activity; or
to B engaging in the activity; or
whether A believes that C consents—
to being present when B engages in the activity; or
to B engaging in the activity.
For the purposes of subsection (1), when B engages in an activity, C may be present—
in person; or
by means of an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000 that is received by C in real time or close to real time.
It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as C was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that C was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as A was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.
An exception applies to this offence—see section 49U.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 49W.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the activity was not sexual or that causing or allowing C to be present when B engages in the activity was not contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct is not a defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.
See sections 5A and 5B of the Sentencing Act 1991 as to standard sentences.

history.raw: Note 4 to s. 49H inserted by No. 34/2017 s. 31(2).

nodes.heading: Causing a child aged 16 or 17 under care, supervision or authority to be present during sexual activity

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
another person (B) engages in an activity; and
the activity is sexual; and
another person (C) is present when B engages in the activity; and
A intentionally causes or allows C to be present when B engages in the activity; and
C is—
a child aged 16 or 17 years; and
under A's care, supervision or authority; and
A's causing or allowing C to be present when B engages in the activity is contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
Whether or not causing or allowing C to be present when B engages in the activity is contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct depends on the circumstances.
For the purposes of subsection (3)—
the circumstances include—
the purpose of the activity; and
whether A seeks or gets sexual arousal or sexual gratification from B engaging in the activity or from the presence of C;
the circumstances do not include—
whether C consents—
to being present when B engages in the activity; or
to B engaging in the activity; or
whether A believes that C consents—
to being present when B engages in the activity; or
to B engaging in the activity.
For the purposes of subsection (1), when B engages in an activity, C may be present—
in person; or
by means of an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000 that is received by C in real time or close to real time.
It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as C was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that C was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as A was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.
An exception applies to this offence—see section 49Y.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 49X, 49Z and 49ZA.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the activity was not sexual or that causing or allowing C to be present when B engages in the activity was not contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct is not a defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Persistent sexual abuse of a child under the age of 16

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A sexually abuses another person (B) on at least 3 occasions during a particular period; and
B is a child under the age of 16 years during the whole of that period.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 2 imprisonment (25 years maximum).
The standard sentence for an offence against subsection (1) is 10 years.
It is not necessary that the alleged acts be of a similar nature or constitute an offence under the same provision.

It is not necessary to prove conduct constituting sexual abuse with the same degree of specificity as to date, time, place, circumstances or occasion as would be required if the accused were charged with an offence constituted by that conduct instead of an offence against subsection (1).
For the purposes of subsection (1), A sexually abuses B if A engages in conduct that would involve the commission by A of any of the following—
an offence against a provision of Subdivision
(rape, sexual assault and associated sexual offences);
an offence against section 49A(1) (sexual penetration of a child under the age of 12);
an offence against section 49B(1) (sexual penetration of a child under the age of 16);
an offence against section 49D(1) (sexual assault of a child under the age of 16);
an offence against section 49F(1) (sexual activity in the presence of a child under the age of 16);
an offence against section 49H(1) (causing a child under the age of 16 to be present during sexual activity);
an offence against a provision of Subdivision
(incest).
Nothing in this section affects the operation of any exception or defence applicable or available to A in respect of the offence constituting the sexual abuse.

If, on the trial of A for an offence against subsection (1), the jury is not satisfied that A is guilty of that offence but is satisfied that A engaged in conduct during the particular period that constitutes one or more instances of an offence against a provision referred to in subsection (5)—
the jury—
must find A not guilty of the offence against subsection (1); and
may find A guilty of the one or more instances of an offence against a provision referred to in subsection (5); and
A is liable to the penalty for any offence of which, in accordance with this subsection, A is found guilty.
Subsection (7) does not restrict the operation of section 239 of the Criminal Procedure Act 2009.
A prosecution for an offence under subsection (1) must not be commenced without the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
See sections 5A and 5B of the Sentencing Act 1991 as to standard sentences.

history.raw: Note to s. 49J inserted by No. 65/2016 s. 24(2), substituted as Notes by No. 34/2017 s. 32(2).

nodes.text: An offence against subsection (1) is a category 1 offence under the Sentencing Act 1991. See section 5(2G) of that Act for the requirement to impose a custodial order for this offence.

nodes.heading: Encouraging a child under the age of 16 to engage in, or be involved in, sexual activity

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A is 18 years of age or more; and
A encourages another person (B) to engage in, or be involved in, an activity; and
the activity is sexual; and
B is a child under the age of 16 years; and
A seeks or gets sexual arousal or sexual gratification from—
the encouragement; or
the sexual activity that is encouraged.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1) encouraging may be done—
in person; or
by means of an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000.
It is not necessary to prove—
that B in fact engaged in, or was involved in, the sexual activity that was encouraged; or
that any sexual activity that B engaged in, or was involved in, was the same activity that was encouraged; or
if B in fact engaged in, or was involved in, sexual activity (whether or not the same activity that was encouraged)—that A was present during that activity.
Despite anything to the contrary in Division 12, it is not an offence for a person to attempt to commit an offence against subsection (1).
It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as B was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that B was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as A was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.
In this section—

nodes.heading: encourage
nodes.text: includes suggest, request, urge and demand.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 49W.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the activity was not sexual is not a defence to this offence— see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Encouraging a child aged 16 or 17 under care, supervision or authority to engage in, or be involved in, sexual activity

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A is 18 years of age or more; and
A encourages another person (B) to engage in, or be involved in, an activity; and
the activity is sexual; and
B is—
a child aged 16 or 17 years; and
under A's care, supervision or authority; and
A seeks or gets sexual arousal or sexual gratification from—
the encouragement; or
the sexual activity that is encouraged.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1) encouraging may be done—
in person; or
by means of an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000.
It is not necessary to prove—
that B in fact engaged in, or was involved in, the sexual activity that was encouraged; or
that any sexual activity that B engaged in, or was involved in, was the same activity that was encouraged; or
if B in fact engaged in, or was involved in, sexual activity (whether or not the same activity that was encouraged)—that A was present during that activity.
Despite anything to the contrary in Division 12, it is not an offence for a person to attempt to commit an offence against subsection (1).
It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as B was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that B was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as A was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.
In this section—

nodes.heading: encourage
nodes.text: includes suggest, request, urge and demand.
An exception applies to this offence—see section 49Y.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 49X, 49Z and 49ZA.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the activity was not sexual is not a defence to this offence— see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Grooming for sexual conduct with a child under the age of 16

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A is 18 years of age or more; and
A communicates, by words or conduct (whether or not a response is made to the communication), with—
another person (B) who is a child under the age of 16 years; or
another person (C) under whose care, supervision or authority B is; and
A intends that the communication facilitate B engaging or being involved in the commission of a sexual offence by A or by another person who is 18 years of age or more.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).

A does not intend to facilitate B engaging or being involved in the commission of a sexual offence by A or by another person who is 18 years of age or more if, were the conduct constituting the sexual offence to occur, A or the other person would satisfy an exception, or have a defence, to that sexual offence.

It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as B or C was, or B and C were, in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that B or C was, or B and C were, outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as A was in Victoria at the time that conduct occurred.
It is immaterial that A, B and C were all outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection
occurred, so long as A intended that the sexual offence would occur in Victoria.
In this section—

nodes.heading: communication
nodes.text: includes an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000;

nodes.heading: sexual offence
nodes.text: means—
an offence against a provision of Subdivision (8A), this Subdivision (other than section 49K(1) or this section), (8C), (8D), (8E), (8F) or (8FA); or
an attempt to commit an offence covered by paragraph (a); or
an assault with intent to commit an offence referred to in paragraph (a).

nodes.heading: Loitering near schools etc. by sexual offender

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A has been found guilty of a relevant offence; and
A loiters at or near a place; and
the place is—
a school, a children's service centre or an education and care service premises; or
a public place within the meaning of the Summary Offences Act 1966 regularly frequented by children and in which children are present at the time of the loitering; and
A knows that the place is—
a school, a children's service centre or an education and care service premises; or
a public place within the meaning of the Summary Offences Act 1966 regularly frequented by children and in which children are present at the time of the loitering.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
In this section—

nodes.heading: children's services centre
nodes.text: means a place at which a children's service within the meaning of the Children's Services Act 1996 operates;

nodes.heading: education and care service premises
nodes.text: means a place at which an education and care service (other than a family day care service) within the meaning of the Education and Care Services National Law (Victoria) educates or cares for children;

nodes.heading: relevant offence
nodes.text: means—

history.raw: S. 49N(3) def. of relevant offence amended by No. 7/2022 s. 40(a).

nodes.text: a sexual offence; or
murder where there are reasonable grounds to believe that a sexual offence was also committed on the victim; or
an offence against—
section 5, 6, 7 or 11 of the Sex Work Act 1994 despite its repeal by the Sex Work Decriminalisation Act 2022; or
section 6, 7, 8 or 9 of the Prostitution Regulation Act 1986; or

section 59(1)(a) or (b) or 60 inserted in this Act on 1 March 1981 by section 5 of the Crimes (Sexual Offences) Act 1980 and repealed on 5 August 1991 by section 3 of the Crimes (Sexual Offences) Act 1991; or
section 19 of the Summary Offences Act 1966; or
any of the following provisions as in force at any time before its repeal—
section 60A of the Classification of Films and Publications Act 1990;
section 57A of the Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) (Enforcement) Act 1995;
section 168A, 168B or 168C of the Police Offences Act 1958; or

a provision referred to in paragraphs (dam), (dama) or (dan) of clause 1 of Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 1991 or of attempting to commit an offence against a provision referred to in paragraph (dama); or
section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) or of attempting to commit an offence against section 51C(1);

nodes.heading: sexual offence
nodes.text: means—

history.raw: S. 49N(3) def. of sexual offence amended by No. 7/2022 s. 40(b).

nodes.text: an offence against a provision referred to in clause 7A, 7B, 8, 9, 10, 11A 11B, 11D(b), 11D(c), 11D(d), 11D(g), 11D(h), 11E, 11F or 12 of Schedule 8; or

an offence against section 44(1), (2) or (4) (incest) as inserted in the Crimes Act 1958 on 5 August 1991 by section 3 of the Crimes (Sexual Offences) Act 1991 and repealed by section 16 of the Crimes Amendment (Sexual Offences) Act 2016; or
an offence of conspiracy to commit, incitement to commit or attempting to commit an offence referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c).

If A has at any time been found guilty of an offence against a law of another State or a Territory of the Commonwealth which creates an offence substantially similar to a sexual offence, that finding of guilt must be taken for the purposes of this section to be a finding of guilt of a sexual offence.
An exception applies to this offence—see section 49ZB.

nodes.heading: Failure by a person in authority to protect a child from a sexual offence

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A occupies a position within, or in relation to, a relevant organisation; and
there is a substantial risk that a relevant child will become the victim of a sexual offence committed by another person who is—
18 years of age or more; and
a person associated with the relevant organisation; and
A knows that the risk exists; and
A, by reason of A's position, has the power or responsibility to reduce or remove that risk; and
A negligently fails to reduce or remove that risk.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).

For the purposes of subsection (1), a person negligently fails to reduce or remove a risk if that failure involves a great falling short of the standard of care that a reasonable person would exercise in the circumstances.
For the avoidance of doubt, in a prosecution for an offence against subsection (1), it is not necessary to prove that a sexual offence has been committed.

It is immaterial that some or all of the circumstances constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as the relevant child was in Victoria at any time while the substantial risk referred to in subsection (1)(b) existed.

It is immaterial that both A and the relevant child were outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the circumstances constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as the sexual offence was at risk of occurring in Victoria.
In this section—

nodes.heading: person associated
nodes.text: , in relation to a relevant organisation, includes but is not limited to a person who is an officer, employee, manager, owner, volunteer, contractor or agent of the organisation but does not include a person only because the person receives services from the organisation;

nodes.heading: relevant child
nodes.text: means a child (whether identifiable or not) under the age of 16 years who is, or may come, under the care, supervision or authority of a relevant organisation;

nodes.heading: relevant organisation
nodes.text: means—
an organisation that exercises care, supervision or authority over children, whether as its primary function or otherwise, and includes but is not limited to—
a church; and
a religious body; and
a school; and
an education and care service within the meaning of the Education and Care Services National Law (Victoria); and
a children's service within the meaning of the Children's Services Act 1996; and
an out of home care service within the meaning of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005; and
a hospital; and
a government department; and
a government agency; and
a municipal council; and
a public sector body; and
a sporting group; and
a youth organisation; and
a charity or benevolent organisation; or

an organisation that, in accordance with an agreement or arrangement with an organisation referred to in paragraph (a), is required or permitted to engage in activities associated with the care, supervision or authority over children exercised by the organisation referred to in paragraph (a);

nodes.heading: sexual offence
nodes.text: means—
an offence against a provision of Subdivision (8A), this Subdivision (other than this section), (8C), (8D), (8E), (8F) or (8FA); or
an attempt to commit an offence covered by paragraph (a) (other than section 49K); or
an assault with intent to commit an offence covered by paragraph (a).

nodes.heading: Abduction or detention of a child under the age of 16 for a sexual purpose

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A—
takes away or detains another person (B); or
causes B to be taken away or detained by another person; and
B is a child under the age of 16 years; and
the person who has lawful charge of B (C) does not consent to B being taken away or detained; and
A knows that—
B is a child under the age of 16 years; or
B is probably a child under the age of 16 years; and
A knows that—
C does not consent to B being taken away or detained; or
C probably does not consent to B being taken away or detained; and
A intends B will take part in a sexual act with A or another person or both; and

B taking part in the sexual act would involve the commission by A, or the other person, or both, of an offence against section 38(1), 39(1), 40(1), 41(1) or a provision of this Subdivision (other than this section).
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
See section 35C for the meaning of taking part in a sexual act.

nodes.heading: Causing or allowing a sexual performance involving a child

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally causes or allows another person (B) to take part in a sexual performance; and
the sexual performance occurs in circumstances that involve any person receiving payment, reward or other benefit (whether before or after the performance) in respect of the performance; and
B is a child under the age of 18 years.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
In this section—

nodes.heading: sexual performance
nodes.text: means a live performance (whether in person or by an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000) that is, or could reasonably be considered to be, for the sexual arousal or sexual gratification of any person.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 49X.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the sexual performance did not occur in circumstances that involved payment, reward or other benefit to any person is not a defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Inviting or offering a sexual performance involving a child

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—
invites another person (B) to take part in a sexual performance; or
offers to a third person that B will take part in a sexual performance; and
the invitation or offer involves any person receiving payment, reward or other benefit (whether before or after the performance) in respect of the performance; and
B is a child under the age of 18 years.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
In this section—

nodes.heading: sexual performance
nodes.text: means a live performance (whether in person or by an electronic communication within the meaning of the Electronic Transactions (Victoria) Act 2000) that is, or could reasonably be considered to be, for the sexual arousal or sexual gratification of any person.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 49X.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that the invitation or offer did not involve payment, reward or other benefit to any person is not a defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Facilitating a sexual offence against a child

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A engages in conduct that aids, facilitates or contributes in any way to another person (B) engaging in sexual conduct (whether or not in Victoria) in relation to a child; and
A engages in the conduct with the intention of obtaining a benefit for A or another person (C); and
A—
intends that the conduct will aid, facilitate or contribute in any way to B engaging in sexual conduct in relation to a child; or
knows that the conduct will, or probably will, aid, facilitate or contribute in any way to B engaging in sexual conduct in relation to a child; and
B's engaging in sexual conduct in relation to a child—
constitutes an offence against section 38(1), 39(1), 40(1), 41(1) or a provision of this Subdivision (other than this section); or
constitutes an offence against a provision of Division 272 of Chapter 8 of the Criminal Code of the Commonwealth; or

takes place outside Victoria but would, if the conduct occurred in Victoria, constitute an offence against a provision covered by subparagraph (i) whether or not it constitutes an offence in the place in which it takes place.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 3 imprisonment (20 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1), conduct that aids, facilitates or contributes in any way to another person engaging in sexual conduct in relation to a child includes—
making travel arrangements; and
causing or allowing a child to enter or remain on premises which A owns, occupies, manages or assists in managing.

A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that B's engaging in sexual conduct in relation to a child did not constitute an offence or, if the conduct takes place outside Victoria, would not constitute an offence, is not a defence to this offence—see section 49ZC.

nodes.heading: Exception to sexual penetration offences—medical or hygienic purposes
nodes.text: A does not commit an offence against section 49A(1), 49B(1) or 49C(1) if A's conduct occurs in the course of a procedure carried out in good faith for medical or hygienic purposes.
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in sections 49A, 49B and 49C.

nodes.heading: Exceptions to offences against children under 16— similarity in age

nodes.text: A does not commit an offence against section 49D(1) or 49F(1) if, at the time at which the offence is alleged to have been committed—
A is not more than 2 years older than B; and
B is 12 years of age or more.
A does not commit an offence against section 49H(1) if, at the time at which the offence is alleged to have been committed—
A is not more than 2 years older than C; and
C is 12 years of age or more.
References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same A, B and C referred to in sections 49D, 49F and 49H.

nodes.heading: Defence to offence against a child under 16— similarity in age
nodes.text: It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49B(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence—
A was not more than 2 years older than B; and
B was 12 years of age or more; and
B consented to the sexual penetration.
References to A and B in this section are references to the same A and B referred to in section 49B.

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children under 16— reasonable belief as to age

nodes.text: It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49B(1), 49D(1) or 49F(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence—
B was 12 years of age or more; and
A reasonably believed that B was 16 years of age or more.
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49H(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence—
C was 12 years of age or more; and
A reasonably believed that C was 16 years of age or more.
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49K(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence, A reasonably believed that B was 16 years of age or more.
A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection
References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same A, B and C referred to in sections 49B, 49D, 49F, 49H and 49K.
Whether or not A reasonably believed that B or C was
years of age or more depends on the circumstances. The circumstances include any steps that A took to find out B or C's age.
An evidential burden applies to the matters referred to in subsections (1)(a) and (2)(a).

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children aged 16 or 17 or under 18—reasonable belief as to age

nodes.text: It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence, A reasonably believed that B was 18 years of age or more.
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49I(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence, A reasonably believed that C was 18 years of age or more.
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49Q(1) or 49R(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence—
B was 12 years of age or more; and
A reasonably believed that B was 18 years of age or more.
A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection
References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I, 49L, 49Q and 49R.
Whether or not A reasonably believed that B or C was
years of age or more depends on the circumstances. The circumstances include any steps that A took to find out B or C's age.
An evidential burden applies to the matter referred to in subsection (3)(a).

nodes.heading: Exceptions to offences against children aged 16 or 17—marriage or domestic partnership

nodes.text: A does not commit an offence against section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1) if, at the time at which the offence is alleged to have been committed—
A and B are married to each other and the marriage is recognised as valid under the Marriage Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—
is not more than 5 years older than B; and
is B's domestic partner and the domestic partnership commenced before B came under A's care, supervision or authority.
A does not commit an offence against section 49I(1) if, at the time at which the offence is alleged to have been committed—
A and C are married to each other and the marriage is recognised as valid under the Marriage Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—
is not more than 5 years older than C; and
is C's domestic partner and the domestic partnership commenced before C came under A's care, supervision or authority.
References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I and 49L.

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children aged 16 or 17—reasonable belief as to marriage or domestic partnership

nodes.text: It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence—
A reasonably believed that A and B were married to each other and that the marriage was recognised as valid under the Marriage Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—
was not more than 5 years older than B; and
reasonably believed that A was B's domestic partner and that the domestic partnership commenced before B came under A's care, supervision or authority.
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49I(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence—
A reasonably believed that A and C were married to each other and that the marriage was recognised as valid under the Marriage Act 1961 of the Commonwealth; or
A—
was not more than 5 years older than C; and
reasonably believed that A was C's domestic partner and that the domestic partnership commenced before C came under A's care, supervision or authority.
A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection
(a) or (b)(ii) or (2)(a) or (b)(ii).
References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I and 49L.
An evidential burden applies to the matters referred to in subsections (1)(b)(i) and (2)(b)(i).

nodes.heading: Defences to offences against children aged 16 or 17—reasonable belief as to care, supervision or authority

nodes.text: It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49C(1), 49E(1), 49G(1) or 49L(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence, A reasonably believed that B was not under A's care, supervision or authority.

It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 49I(1) if, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence, A reasonably believed that C was not under A's care, supervision or authority.
A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection
References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same A, B and C referred to in sections 49C, 49E, 49G, 49I and 49L.

nodes.heading: Exception to loitering offence
nodes.text: A does not commit an offence against section 49N(1) if A has a reasonable excuse for loitering at or near a place referred to in section 49N(1)(c).
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in section 49N.

nodes.heading: No defence of mistaken but honest and reasonable belief of certain matters
nodes.text: It is not a defence to a charge that, at the time of the conduct constituting the offence, A was under a mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that—
for an offence against section 49A(1)— B was 12 years of age or more; or
for an offence against section 49D(1) or 49E(1)—the touching was not—
sexual; or
contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct; or
for an offence against section 49F(1) or 49G(1)—
the activity was not sexual; or
engaging in the activity in the presence of B was not contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct; or
for an offence against section 49H(1) or 49I(1)—
the activity was not sexual; or
A's causing or allowing C to be present when B engages in the activity was not contrary to community standards of acceptable conduct; or
for an offence against section 49K(1) or 49L(1)—the activity was not sexual; or
for an offence against section 49Q(1)— the sexual performance did not occur in circumstances that involved payment, reward or other benefit to any person in respect of the performance; or
for an offence against section 49R(1)— the invitation or offer did not involve payment, reward or other benefit to any person in respect of the performance; or

for an offence against section 49S(1)— B's engaging in sexual conduct in relation to a child did not constitute an offence or, if the conduct takes place outside Victoria, would not constitute an offence.
References to A, B and C in this section are references to the same A, B and C referred to in sections 49A, 49D, 49E, 49F, 49G, 49H, 49I, 49K, 49L, 49Q, 49R and 49S.

nodes.heading: Definitions
nodes.text: In this Subdivision—

nodes.heading: child
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means—
the person's child by birth; or
the person's genetic child; or
the person's child by operation of the Adoption Act 1984; or
the person's child by operation of the Status of Children Act 1974;

nodes.heading: half-sibling
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means a person who shares a common parent with the person;

nodes.heading: lineal ancestor
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means a lineal ancestor of the person's parent;

nodes.heading: lineal descendant
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means a lineal descendant of the person's child;

nodes.heading: parent
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means—
the person's birth parent; or
the person's genetic parent; or
the person's parent by operation of the Adoption Act 1984; or
the person's parent by operation of the Status of Children Act 1974;

nodes.heading: sibling
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means a person who has the same parents as the person;

nodes.heading: step-parent
nodes.text: , in relation to a person, means the spouse or domestic partner of the person's parent, being a person who is not the person's parent.

nodes.heading: Rebuttable presumption as to family relationship
nodes.text: In a proceeding for an offence against a provision of this Subdivision, there is a rebuttable presumption that—
A knows that A is related to B in the way alleged; and
people who are reputed to be related to each other in a particular way are in fact related in that way.

nodes.heading: Sexual penetration of a child or lineal descendant

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—
sexually penetrates another person (B); or
causes or allows B to sexually penetrate A; and
B is A's child or lineal descendant; and
A knows that B is A's child or lineal descendant.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 2 imprisonment (25 years maximum).
The standard sentence for an offence against subsection (1) is 10 years if B is, at the time of the offence, under the age of 18 years.
An exception applies to this offence—see section 50G.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.
See sections 5A and 5B of the Sentencing Act 1991 as to standard sentences.

history.raw: Note 4 to s. 50C inserted by No. 65/2016 s. 24(3), substituted by No. 34/2017 s. 33(2).

nodes.text: An offence against subsection (1) is a category 1 offence under the Sentencing Act 1991 if B is, at the time of the offence, under the age of 18 years. See section 5(2G) of that Act for the requirement to impose a custodial order for this offence.

history.raw: Note 5 to s. 50C inserted by No. 34/2017 s. 33(2).

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—
sexually penetrates another person (B); or
causes or allows B to sexually penetrate A; and
B is a child or lineal descendant of A's spouse or domestic partner; and
A knows that B is a child or lineal descendant of A's spouse or domestic partner.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 2 imprisonment (25 years maximum).
The standard sentence for an offence against subsection (1) is 10 years if B is, at the time of the offence, under the age of 18 years.
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 50G and 50I.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.
See sections 5A and 5B of the Sentencing Act 1991 as to standard sentences.

history.raw: Note 4 to s. 50D inserted by No. 65/2016 s. 24(4), substituted by No. 34/2017 s. 34(2).

nodes.text: An offence against subsection (1) is a category 1 offence under the Sentencing Act 1991 if B is, at the time of the offence, under the age of 18 years. See section 5(2G) of that Act for the requirement to impose a custodial order for this offence.

history.raw: Note 5 to s. 50D inserted by No. 34/2017 s. 34(2).

nodes.heading: Sexual penetration of a parent, lineal ancestor or step-parent

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—
sexually penetrates another person (B); or
causes or allows B to sexually penetrate A; and
A is 18 years of age or more; and
B is A's parent, lineal ancestor or step-parent; and
A knows that B is A's parent, lineal ancestor or step-parent.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 50G and 50J.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.

nodes.heading: Sexual penetration of a sibling or half-sibling

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally—
sexually penetrates another person (B); or
causes or allows B to sexually penetrate A; and
B is A's sibling or half-sibling; and
A knows that B is A's sibling or half-sibling.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
An exception applies to this offence—see section 50G.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 50H.
B's consent is not a defence to this offence—see section 50K.

nodes.heading: Exception—medical or hygienic purposes
nodes.text: A does not commit an offence against a provision of this Subdivision if A's conduct occurs in the course of a procedure carried out in good faith for medical or hygienic purposes.
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in the offence provisions in this Subdivision.

nodes.heading: Defence—accused did not consent
nodes.text: It is a defence to a charge for an offence against a provision of this Subdivision if A did not consent to the conduct constituting the offence.
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in the offence provisions in this Subdivision.

A person may intentionally engage in conduct but not consent to it—see section 36AA. For example, B threatens to hurt A if A does not allow B to sexually penetrate A. A intentionally allows B to sexually penetrate A because A is afraid of harm. A did not consent to the conduct constituting the offence.

history.raw: Note 2 to s. 50H amended by No. 38/2022 s. 12.

nodes.heading: Exception to offences against section 50D
nodes.text: A does not commit an offence against section 50D(1) if, at the time at which the offence is alleged to have been committed—
B is 18 years of age or more; and
A has not engaged in sexual activity with B when B was under 18 years of age; and
B has not at any time been under A's care, supervision or authority.
References to A and B in this section are references to the same A and B referred to in section 50D.
A does not commit an offence against section 50E(1) if, at the time at which the offence is alleged to have been committed—
B is A's step-parent; and
A has not at any time been under B's care, supervision or authority.
A does not commit an offence against section 50E(1) if B engaged in sexual activity with A when A was under 18 years of age.
References to A and B in this section are references to the same A and B referred to in section 50E.

nodes.heading: Consent not a defence
nodes.text: It is not a defence to a charge for an offence against a provision of this Subdivision that B consented to the conduct constituting the offence.
The reference to B in this section is a reference to the same B referred to in the offence provisions in this Subdivision.

nodes.text: In this Subdivision—

nodes.heading: administer
nodes.text: , in relation to a website, includes building, developing and maintaining the website but does not include hosting the website;

nodes.heading: authorised classifier
nodes.text: means a person, or a person who belongs to a class of person, prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this definition;

nodes.heading: child
nodes.text: means a person under the age of 18 years;

nodes.heading: child abuse material
nodes.text: means material that—
depicts or describes—
a person who is, or who appears or is implied to be, a child—
as a victim of torture, cruelty or physical abuse (whether or not the torture, cruelty or abuse is sexual); or
as a victim of sexual abuse; or
engaged in, or apparently engaging in, a sexual pose or sexual activity (whether or not in the presence of another person); or
in the presence of another person who is engaged in, or apparently engaged in, a sexual pose or sexual activity; or
the genital or anal region of a person who is, or who appears or is implied to be, a child; or
the breast area of a person who is, or who appears or is implied to be, a female child; and
reasonable persons would regard as being, in the circumstances, offensive;

nodes.heading: child abuse material disposal order
nodes.text: means an order made under section 51X(1);

nodes.heading: child abuse material offence
nodes.text: means an offence against a provision of this Subdivision;

nodes.heading: classified
nodes.text: means classified under the Commonwealth Act;

nodes.heading: Commonwealth Act
nodes.text: means the Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) Act 1995 of the Commonwealth;

nodes.heading: deal
nodes.text: , in relation to child abuse material, includes any of the following—
viewing, uploading or downloading child abuse material;
making child abuse material available for viewing, uploading or downloading;
facilitating the viewing, uploading or downloading of child abuse material;

nodes.heading: distribute
nodes.text: , in relation to material, includes—

history.raw: S. 51A(1) def. of distribute inserted by No. 38/2022 s. 20(1).

nodes.text: publishing the material; and
exhibiting, communicating, sending, supplying or transmitting the material to any other person; and
making the material available for access by any other person;

nodes.heading: electronic material
nodes.text: includes data from which text, images or sound may be generated;

nodes.heading: encourage
nodes.text: includes suggest, request, urge and demand;

nodes.heading: law enforcement agency
nodes.text: means—
Victoria Police or the police force or police service of any other State or of the Northern Territory of Australia; or
the Australian Federal Police; or
the Australian Crime Commission established by the Australian Crime Commission Act 2002 of the Commonwealth; or
any other authority or person responsible for the enforcement of the laws of—
Victoria or any other State; or
the Commonwealth; or
the Australian Capital Territory; or
the Northern Territory of Australia;

nodes.heading: material
nodes.text: means—
any film, audio, photograph, printed matter, image, computer game or text; or
any electronic material; or
any other thing of any kind;
See also subsection (2).

nodes.heading: police officer
nodes.text: includes a member of the Australian Federal Police;

nodes.heading: relevant industry regulatory authority
nodes.text: means a person or body prescribed to be a relevant industry regulatory authority for the purposes of section 51S(2)(d);

nodes.heading: seized thing
nodes.text: means a thing that came into the possession of a police officer in the course of the exercise of functions as a police officer;

nodes.heading: website
nodes.text: includes a page, or a group of pages, on the Internet.
For the purposes of this Subdivision, an image may be still, moving, recorded or unrecorded.

nodes.heading: Involving a child in the production of child abuse material

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally involves another person (B) in the production of material; and
B is a child; and
A knows that B is, or probably is, a child; and
the material is child abuse material; and
A knows that the material is, or probably is, child abuse material.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1), the ways in which A involves B in the production of material may include—
inviting or encouraging B to be involved, or offering B to be involved, in the production of the material; or
causing or allowing B to be involved in the production of the material; or
using B in the production of the material.
B need not be described or depicted in the material.
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 51J, 51K and 51M.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 51L, 51N, 51O, 51P, 51Q and 51R.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.
A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally produces material; and
the material is child abuse material; and
A knows that the material is, or probably is, child abuse material.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1), the ways in which material is produced may include—
filming, printing, photographing, recording, writing, drawing or otherwise generating material; or
altering or manipulating material; or
reproducing or copying material.
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 51J, 51K and 51M.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 51L, 51N, 51O, 51P, 51Q and 51R.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.
A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally distributes material; and
the material is child abuse material; and
A knows that the material is, or probably is, child abuse material.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
It is not necessary to prove—
the identity of any person to whom the material was distributed; or
that another person in fact accessed the material.
It is immaterial that some or all of the child abuse material was distributed outside Victoria, so long as A was in Victoria at some or all of the time at which the material was distributed.
It is immaterial that A was outside Victoria at some or all of time at which the material was distributed, so long as some or all of the material was distributed in Victoria.
See section 51A(1) for the meaning of distribute.

history.raw: Note 1 to s. 51D amended by No. 38/2022 s. 21.

nodes.text: Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 51J, 51K and 51M.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 51L, 51P, 51Q and 51R.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.

nodes.heading: Administering a website used to deal with child abuse material

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A administers, or assists in the administration of, a website; and
the website is used by another person to deal with child abuse material; and
A—
intends that the website be used by another person to deal with child abuse material; or
is aware that the website is being used by another person to deal with child abuse material.

1 A manages membership of a website. A intends that the website be used by other persons to view child abuse material. 2 A monitors traffic through a website and ensures that the web server hardware and software are running correctly. A is aware that the website is being used by other persons to download child abuse material.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
It is not necessary to prove the identity of the person using the website to deal with child abuse material.

It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria or that a computer or device used in connection with administering the website was outside Victoria, so long as—
the person using the website to deal with child abuse material was in Victoria; or
the computer or device used to deal with child abuse material was in Victoria.

It is immaterial that the person using the website to deal with child abuse material was outside Victoria or that the computer or device used to deal with child abuse material was outside Victoria, so long as—
some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred in Victoria; or
a computer or device used in connection with administering the website was in Victoria.
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 51J, 51K and 51S.
Defences apply to this offence—see section 51L.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.

nodes.heading: Encouraging use of a website to deal with child abuse material

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A is 18 years of age or more; and
A encourages another person to use a website; and
A intends that the other person use the website to deal with child abuse material.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
In determining whether A has encouraged another person to use a website to deal with child abuse material, it is not necessary to prove—
the identity of the person encouraged to use the website to deal with child abuse material; or
that another person in fact used the website to deal with child abuse material; or
if another person did in fact use the website to deal with child abuse material, that it was A's encouragement that caused the person to do so.
Despite anything to the contrary in Division 12, it is not an offence for a person to attempt to commit an offence against subsection (1).

It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as the person being encouraged was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.

It is immaterial that the person being encouraged was outside Victoria at the time the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as some or all of that conduct occurred in Victoria.

If an adult uses a child as an innocent agent to encourage another person to use a website, intending that the other person use the website to deal with child abuse material, the adult commits an offence against subsection (1).
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 51J and 51K.
A defence applies to this offence—see section 51L.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.
A person (A) commits an offence if A knowingly possesses child abuse material.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).

For the purposes of subsection (1), A possesses child abuse material that is electronic material if A controls access to the material whether or not A has physical possession of the electronic material.

It is immaterial that the electronic material was outside Victoria, so long as A was in Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred.

It is immaterial that A was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred, so long as the electronic material was in Victoria.

1 A has an online storage account for electronic material accessible with a username and password. A has control of what is stored in the account and can move material around within the account or delete material from the account. A has an electronic folder in the account that A has titled 'personal' in which A puts some electronic child abuse material. A knowingly has possession of child abuse material. 2 In an online chat A is given a password for a joint email account that is shared with multiple users that A doesn't know. A logs into the email account and views emails that contain child abuse material images. While logged in A has the ability to view, move or delete emails that contain child abuse material. A continues to access the email account to view images. A knowingly has possession of child abuse material.
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 51J, 51K and 51M.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 51L, 51N, 51O, 51P, 51Q, 51R and 51T.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.
A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally accesses material; and
the material is child abuse material; and
A knows that the material is, or probably is, child abuse material.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
For the purposes of subsection (1), the ways in which A accesses material may include—
viewing material; or
displaying material by an electronic medium or any other output of the material by an electronic medium.
Exceptions apply to this offence—see sections 51J, 51K and 51M.
Defences apply to this offence—see sections 51L, 51N, 51O, 51P, 51Q and 51R.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.

nodes.heading: Assisting a person to avoid apprehension

nodes.text: A person (A) commits an offence if—
A intentionally provides information to another person (B); and

A intends that B use the information for the purpose of avoiding or reducing the likelihood of apprehension for an offence committed by B against section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51E(1), 51F(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1).

1 A provides information to B about how to use a website to deal with child abuse material anonymously or how to encrypt electronic material containing child abuse material. 2 A provides information to B about how to delete electronic material that records information about B's identity.
A person who commits an offence against subsection (1) is liable to level 5 imprisonment (10 years maximum).
It is not necessary to prove—
the identity of the person to whom the information was provided; or
that the information was actually used by the other person.

It is immaterial that some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection (1) occurred outside Victoria, so long as the other person was in Victoria at the time at which that conduct occurred.
It is immaterial that the other person was outside Victoria at the time at which some or all of the conduct constituting an offence against subsection
occurred, so long as that conduct occurred in Victoria.

For the purposes of subsections (4) and (5), information is provided by A to B at the place where A is at the time of giving that information irrespective of where B is at the time of receiving that information.
A mistaken but honest and reasonable belief that reasonable persons would not regard the child abuse material as offensive is not a defence to this offence—see section 51U.

nodes.heading: Exception—administration of the law
nodes.text: A does not commit a child abuse material offence (other than an offence against section 51I(1)) if the conduct is engaged in by A in good faith in the course of official duties of A—
connected with the administration of the criminal justice system, including the investigation or prosecution of offences; or
as an employee of the Department of Justice and Regulation who is authorised to engage in that conduct by the Secretary to that Department.
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in the child abuse material offence provisions.

nodes.heading: Exception—classification
nodes.text: A does not commit a child abuse material offence (other than an offence against section 51I(1)) in respect of material that, at the time at which the offence is alleged to have been committed, was classified other than RC or would, if classified, have been classified other than RC.
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in the child abuse material offence provisions.
Under the Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) Act 1995 of the Commonwealth, a classification of RC means Refused Classification.

nodes.heading: Defence of artistic merit or public benefit

nodes.text: It is a defence to a charge for a child abuse material offence (other than an offence against section 51I(1)) if—
the material—
was not produced with the involvement of a person who was, at the time it was produced, under the age of 18 years; and
possesses artistic merit; or
the material is of public benefit.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(b), material that is of public benefit includes material that is for a genuine medical, legal, scientific or educational purpose.

1 A is a university lecturer in psychology. During a lecture on abnormal psychology, A shows a lecture slide with examples of textual child abuse material to illustrate the type of material associated with an abnormal psychological profile. The lecture slide is of public benefit. 2 A is a photojournalist in a war zone. A takes a photo of a child victim of torture and submits it to a news organisation for publication. The photo is of public benefit.
A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of probabilities) the matter referred to in subsection
(a)(ii) or (b).
The reference to A in this section is a reference to the same A referred to in the child abuse material offence provisions.
An evidential burden applies to the matter referred to in subsection (1)(a)(i).
A does not commit an offence against section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) if—
A is a child; and
the child abuse material is an image; and
the image depicts A alone.

A is 15 years old and takes a photograph of themselves. A stores the photograph on their mobile phone. The offences in 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) do not apply to A in respect of the image.
Section 51O may apply if A is an adult.
A does not commit an offence against section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) if—
A is a child; and
the child abuse material is an image; and
A is the victim of a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment and the image depicts that offence.
The image depicts the child (A) being raped by another person. The offences in sections 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) and 51H(1) do not apply to A in respect of the image.
In subsections (1) and (2), a reference to an image, in relation to an offence against section 51B(1), is a reference to the image that A involves the child in producing.
References to A in this section are references to the same A referred to in sections 51B, 51C, 51D, 51G and 51H.
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) if—
A is a child; and
the child abuse material is an image; and
the image depicts one or more persons (whether or not it depicts A); and
the image—
does not depict an act that is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment; or
depicts an act that is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment but A reasonably believes that it does not; and
at the time of the conduct constituting the offence—
A was not more than 2 years older than the youngest child depicted in the image; or
A reasonably believed that they were not more than 2 years older than the youngest child depicted in the image.
1 The image depicts A taking part in an act of sexual penetration with another child who is not more than
2 years younger. Both are consenting to the act. A is not guilty of an offence against section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) in respect of the image.

2 The image depicts a child being sexually penetrated. A is a child and A reasonably believes that the image depicts a consensual sexual relationship between two 16 year olds and is therefore not a criminal offence. A also reasonably believes that A is not more than 2 years older than the youngest child depicted in the image. A is not guilty of an offence against section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51D(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) in respect of the image.
In subsection (1), a reference to an image, in relation to an offence against section 51B(1), is a reference to the image that A involves the child in producing.
A bears the burden of proving (on the balance of probabilities) the matters referred to in subsection
(d)(ii) and (e)(ii).
References to A in this section are references to the same A referred to in sections 51B, 51C, 51D, 51G and 51H.
An evidential burden applies to the matters referred to in subsection (1)(a), (b), (c), (d)(i) and (e)(i).
It is a defence to a charge for an offence against section 51B(1), 51C(1), 51G(1) or 51H(1) if—
the child abuse material is an image; and
the image depicts A as a child; and
the image does not depict A committing a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment; and
A does not distribute the image to any other person.
