nodes.heading: Giving name and address on demand

history.raw: Pt 3 Div. 1 Subdiv. (29A) (Heading and s. 456AA) inserted by No. 129/1993 s. 4 (as amended by No. 33/1994 s. 27(5)).

nodes.heading: Requirement to give name and address

history.raw: S. 456AA inserted by No. 129/1993 s. 4 (as amended by No. 33/1994 s. 27(5)).

nodes.text: A police officer or a protective services officer on duty at a designated place may request a person to state his or her name and address if the police officer or the protective services officer believes on reasonable grounds that the person—
has committed or is about to commit an offence, whether indictable or summary; or
may be able to assist in the investigation of an indictable offence which has been committed or is suspected of having been committed.

A police officer or a protective services officer who makes a request under subsection (1) must inform the person of the grounds for his or her belief in sufficient detail to allow the person to understand the nature of the offence or suspected offence.
A person who, in response to a request made by a police officer or a protective services officer in accordance with this section—
refuses or fails to comply with the request; or
states a name that is false in a material particular; or
states an address other than the full and correct address of his or her ordinary place of residence or business—
is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by a level 11 fine (5 penalty units maximum).

A person who is requested by a police officer or a protective services officer under subsection (1) to state his or her name and address may request the officer to state, orally or in writing, his or her name, rank and place of duty.
A police officer or a protective services officer who, in response to a request under subsection
refuses or fails to comply with the request; or
states a name or rank that is false in a material particular; or
states as his or her place of duty an address other than the name of the police station which is the police officer's or the protective services officer's ordinary place of duty; or
refuses to comply with the request in writing if requested to do so—
is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by a level 11 fine (5 penalty units maximum).
A protective services officer may only exercise the power under this section in relation to a person who is at, or in the vicinity of, a designated place.
In this section—

nodes.heading: designated place
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in the Victoria Police Act 2013.

nodes.heading: No person to be arrested without warrant except under this Act etc.
nodes.text: After the commencement of the Crimes (Powers of Arrest) Act 1972 no person shall be arrested without warrant except pursuant to the provisions of—
this Act; or
some other Act expressly giving power to arrest without warrant.

nodes.heading: Person found committing offences may be arrested without warrant by any person

history.raw: S. 458 substituted by No. 8247 s. 2, amended by No. 57/1989 s. 3(Sch. item 42.47).

nodes.text: Any person, whether a police officer or not, may at any time without warrant apprehend and take before a bail justice or the Magistrates' Court to be dealt with according to law or deliver to a police officer to be so taken, any person—

history.raw: S. 458(1) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.13).

nodes.text: he finds committing any offence (whether an indictable offence or an offence punishable on summary conviction) where he believes on reasonable grounds that the apprehension of the person is necessary for any one or more of the following reasons, namely—
to ensure the attendance of the offender before a court of competent jurisdiction;

history.raw: S. 458(1)(a)(i) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 40.30).

nodes.text: to preserve public order;
to prevent the continuation or repetition of the offence or the commission of a further offence; or
for the safety or welfare of members of the public or of the offender;
when instructed so to do by any police officer having power under this Act to apprehend that person; or

history.raw: S. 458(1)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.13).

nodes.text: he believes on reasonable grounds is escaping from legal custody or aiding or abetting another person to escape from legal custody or avoiding apprehension by some person having authority to apprehend that person in the circumstances of the case.

history.raw: S. 458(1)(c) amended by No. 117/1986 s. 6(Sch. 1 item 1(8)(a)).

nodes.text: For the purposes of paragraph (a) in subsection (1) offence means offence at common law or a contravention of or failure to comply with a provision of an Act of Parliament and unless otherwise by Act of Parliament expressly provided does not include a contravention of or failure to comply with a rule regulation by-law or other law made under an Act of Parliament.

A person who has been apprehended without warrant pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (a) in subsection (1) in respect of any offence punishable on summary conviction (not being an indictable offence that may be heard and determined summarily) and taken into custody shall be held in the custody of the person apprehending him only so long as any reason referred to in the said paragraph for his apprehension continues and where, before that person is charged with an offence, it appears to the person arresting that person that the reason no longer continues the person arresting that other person shall, without any further or other authority than this subsection, release that person from custody without bail or cause him to be so released and whether or not a summons has been issued against him or a notice to appear has been served on him with respect to the offence alleged.

history.raw: S. 458(3) amended by Nos 9008 s. 2(1)(Sch. item 2(k)), 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 40.31).

nodes.text: In subsection (3), notice to appear has the same meaning as in the Criminal Procedure Act 2009.

nodes.heading: Powers of police officer or protective services officer to apprehend offenders

S. 459 substituted by No. 8247 s. 2, amended by No. 43/2011 s. 17(2)(3) (ILA s. 39B(1)).

nodes.text: he believes on reasonable grounds has committed an indictable offence in Victoria (including any indictable offence which may be heard and determined summarily); or

to be escaping from legal custody; or

nodes.heading: Arrest on reasonable grounds not to be taken to be unlawful

history.raw: S. 461 amended by No. 7546 s. 11, substituted by No. 8247 s. 2.

nodes.text: Where an apprehension is made under a belief on reasonable grounds in accordance with the provisions of section 458 or section 459 the apprehension shall not cease to be lawful or be taken to be unlawful where it subsequently appears or is found that the person apprehended did not commit the offence alleged.

A police officer shall not be bound to take into custody or to take before a bail justice or the Magistrates' Court any person found committing an offence if the police officer believes on reasonable grounds that proceedings can effectively be brought against that person by way of summons or notice to appear.

nodes.heading: Definition of finds committing
nodes.text: In this Act the expression finds committing and any derivative thereof extends to the case of a person found doing any act or so behaving or conducting himself or in such circumstances that the person finding him believes on reasonable grounds that the person so found is guilty of an offence.

nodes.heading: Use of force to prevent the commission of an indictable offence
nodes.text: A person may use such force not disproportionate to the objective as he believes on reasonable grounds to be necessary to prevent the commission, continuance or completion of an indictable offence or to effect or assist in effecting the lawful arrest of a person committing or suspected of committing any offence.

A police officer or protective services officer uses lethal force on a person to prevent that person from committing an indictable offence that involves causing really serious injury or death because the officer believes on reasonable grounds that it is necessary to use that force for that purpose. The police officer or protective services officer may do so before that offence is committed.

history.raw: Example to s. 462A inserted by No. 32/2018 s. 131.

nodes.heading: Arrest of offenders on board aircraft

history.raw: S. 463A inserted by No. 7088 s. 2(e), amended by No. 57/1989 s. 3(Sch. item 42.55).

nodes.text: The person in command of an aircraft may, on board the aircraft, with such assistance as is necessary, arrest without warrant a person whom he finds committing, or reasonably suspects of having committed, or of having attempted to commit, an offence on or in relation to or affecting the use of an aircraft and that person in command or a person authorized by him may hold the person so arrested in custody until he can be brought before a bail justice or the Magistrates' Court or other proper authority to be dealt with in accordance with law.

The person in command of an aircraft may, where he considers it necessary so to do in order to prevent an offence on or in relation to or affecting the use of an aircraft or to avoid danger to the safety of the aircraft or of persons on board the aircraft, with such assistance as he thinks necessary—
place a person who is on board the aircraft under restraint or in custody; and
if the aircraft is not in the course of a flight—remove a person from the aircraft.

nodes.heading: Prevention of suicide
nodes.text: Every person is justified in using such force as may reasonably be necessary to prevent the commission of suicide or of any act which he believes on reasonable grounds would, if committed, amount to suicide.

nodes.text: to practise in the nursing and midwifery profession as a midwife (other than as a student); and
in the register of midwives kept for that profession;

nodes.heading: missing persons index
nodes.text: means an index of DNA profiles, derived from forensic material, of—

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of missing persons index inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.

nodes.text: persons who are missing; and
volunteers who are relatives by blood of missing persons;

nodes.heading: National Criminal Investigation DNA Database
nodes.text: means the DNA database system that—
is known as the National Criminal Investigation DNA Database; and
is managed by the Commonwealth;

nodes.heading: NCIDD
nodes.text: means the National Criminal Investigation DNA Database;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of NCIDD inserted by No. 32/2007 s. 4(2).

nodes.heading: non-intimate part of the body
nodes.text: means any part of the body other than an intimate part;

nodes.heading: non-intimate sample
nodes.text: means—
a sample of hair, other than pubic hair, including the root if required;
a sample of matter taken from under a fingernail or toenail;
a swab, washing or sample taken from any external part of the body other than the genital or anal region of a male or female or the breast of a female;

nodes.heading: nurse
nodes.text: means a person registered under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law to practise in the nursing and midwifery profession as a nurse (other than as a midwife or as a student);

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of nurse inserted by No. 81/1997 s. 16(c), amended by No. 97/2005 s. 182(Sch. 4 item 14.2(c)), substituted by No. 13/2010 s. 51(Sch. item 17.3(c)).

nodes.heading: participating jurisdiction
nodes.text: means the Commonwealth, another State or a Territory in which there is a corresponding law in force;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of participating jurisdiction inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.

nodes.heading: physical examination
nodes.text: means an examination of the external part of a person's body requiring touching of the person or removal of the person's clothing;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of physical examination inserted by No. 129/1993 s. 6(e).

nodes.heading: police custody officer
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in the Victoria Police Act 2013;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of police custody officer inserted by No. 59/2015 s. 25(a).

nodes.heading: police gaol
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in the Corrections Act 1986;

nodes.heading: prison
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in the Corrections Act 1986 but includes a youth justice centre established under section 478 of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of related material and information inserted by No. 81/1997 s. 16(e), amended by Nos 27/2006 ss 3(a), 17(1), 25/2017 s. 50, 3/2019 s. 52(4).

nodes.text: in relation to any DNA profile sample or any sample taken in a forensic procedure conducted in accordance with sections 464R to 464ZA or section 464ZF, 464ZFAAA or 464ZFAB, means notes and audiovisual recordings made of the taking of the DNA profile sample or the conduct of the forensic procedure and any information which may identify the person contained in any record of or report relating to the DNA profile sample or the forensic procedure and in any copy of the record or report;

in relation to any sample voluntarily given by a person in accordance with sections 464ZGB to 464ZGD, means notes and audiovisual recording (if any) made of the procedure to take the sample and any information which may identify the person contained in any record of or report relating to the taking of the sample and in any copy of a record or report;

nodes.heading: relevant suspect
nodes.text: means a person of or above the age of 18 years who—

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of relevant suspect inserted by No. 84/1989 s. 4(b), substituted by No. 23/1991 s. 4(b), amended by Nos 81/1997 s. 16(f), 61/2001 s. 16(1)(a), 16/2002 s. 17(1), 35/2002 s. 28(Sch. item 3.1), 72/2004 s. 24, substituted by No. 72/2013 s. 3(a).
S. 464(2) def. of suspect inserted by No. 38/1988 s. 5(b), amended by Nos 25/1989 s. 14(a), 72/2004 s. 25.

nodes.text: is suspected of having committed or attempted to commit an indictable offence; or
has been charged with an indictable offence;

nodes.heading: responsible Minister
nodes.text: , in relation to a participating jurisdiction means a Minister of that jurisdiction who is responsible for administration of a corresponding law;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of responsible Minister inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.

nodes.heading: responsible person
nodes.text: , in relation to a DNA database, means the person responsible for the care, control and management of the system;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of responsible person inserted by No. 32/2007 s. 4(2).

nodes.heading: security patient
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in the Mental Health and Wellbeing Act 2022;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of security patient inserted by No. 81/1997 s. 16(g), amended by Nos 26/2014 s. 455(Sch. item 7.2(d)), 39/2022 s. 813(c).

nodes.heading: senior police officer
nodes.text: means a police officer of or above the rank of senior sergeant;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of senior police officer inserted by No. 41/2004 s. 8, amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.18(a)(iii)).
S. 464(2) def. of senior police officer authorisation inserted by No. 3/2019 s. 52(1).

nodes.heading: senior police officer authorisation
nodes.text: means an authorisation under section 464ZFAC;

nodes.heading: serious offenders index
nodes.text: means an index of DNA profiles derived from forensic material taken from—

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of serious offenders index inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5, amended by No. 3/2019 s. 52(5).

nodes.text: offenders in accordance with section 464ZF, or under a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction; and
registrable offenders in accordance with section 464ZFAB; and
offenders in accordance with section 464ZFAC(2)(a)(i); and
suspects who have been convicted of—
an offence and an order has been made under section 464ZFB(1); or
an offence and to which section 464ZFB(1AA) applies; or
an offence in respect of which a forensic procedure may be conducted under a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction;

nodes.heading: statistical index
nodes.text: means an index of information that—

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of statistical index inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.

nodes.text: is obtained from the analysis of forensic material taken from persons in accordance with this Subdivision or under a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction; and
has been compiled for statistical purposes; and
cannot be used to discover the identity of persons from whom the forensic material was taken;

nodes.heading: suspect
nodes.text: means a person of or above the age of 18 years who—

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of suspects index inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5, amended by Nos 27/2006 s. 3(b), 3/2019 s. 52(6).

nodes.text: is suspected of having committed an offence; or
has been charged with an offence; or
has been summonsed to answer to a charge;

nodes.heading: suspects index
nodes.text: means an index of DNA profiles derived from forensic material taken from suspects in accordance with section 464R, 464T or 464U, DNA profile samples taken in accordance with section 464SC or 464SE or under a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction or taken from persons found not guilty because of mental impairment in accordance with section 464ZFAAA or section 464ZFAC(2)(a)(ii);

nodes.heading: unknown deceased persons index
nodes.text: means an index of DNA profiles of deceased persons whose identities are unknown where the DNA profile is derived from forensic material;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of unknown deceased persons index inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.

nodes.heading: Victorian DNA database
nodes.text: means the DNA database system kept under section 464ZFD;

nodes.heading: volunteer
nodes.text: means a person who volunteers to give a sample under section 464ZGB;

history.raw: S. 464(2) def. of volunteer inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.
S. 464(2) def. of volunteers (limited purposes) index inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.
S. 464(2) def. of volunteers (unlimited purposes) index inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 5.

nodes.heading: volunteers (limited purposes) index
nodes.text: means an index of DNA profiles derived from forensic material taken from volunteers, under section 464ZGB or a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction, who have chosen that the information obtained from analysis of the material may be used only for a limited purpose that is specified by the volunteer and noted on the index;

nodes.heading: volunteers (unlimited purposes) index
nodes.text: means an index of DNA profiles derived from forensic material taken from volunteers, under section 464ZGB or a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction, who have chosen that the information obtained from analysis of the material may be used for the purpose of a criminal investigation or any other purpose for which the DNA database may be used;

nodes.heading: youth residential centre
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005;

The Minister administering the Victoria Police Act 2013 may appoint by notice published in the Government Gazette a person or class of persons as a person or persons authorised to take fingerprints in accordance with this Subdivision.

history.raw: S. 464(3) inserted by No. 25/1989 s. 11(b). amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.18(b)).

nodes.heading: Digital recordings
nodes.text: If this Subdivision requires an audio recording or an audiovisual recording to be made and the recording is made in a digitised format, the maker of the recording must certify that the recording has not been altered after its making and that the prescribed requirements, if any, in relation to the method of recording have been met.

nodes.heading: Investigating official to ask whether person in custody is an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person
nodes.text: If a person is taken into custody, an investigating official must ask the person whether they are an Aboriginal person or a Torres Strait Islander—

history.raw: S. 464AAB inserted by No. 48/2018 s. 17, amended by No. 26/2023 s. 77(2).

nodes.text: as soon as practicable after the person is taken into custody; and
in any event, before any questioning or investigation under section 464A(2) commences.
Section 464FA requires that the Victorian Aboriginal Legal Service be notified if an Aboriginal person or a Torres Strait Islander is taken into custody.

history.raw: Note to s. 464AAB amended by No. 26/2023 s. 77(3).

nodes.text: Every person taken into custody for an offence (whether committed in Victoria or elsewhere) must be—
released unconditionally; or
released on bail; or
brought before a bail justice or the Magistrates' Court—
within a reasonable time of being taken into custody.
Section 10 of the Bail Act 1977 applies at the expiration of the reasonable time referred to in subsection (1).

history.raw: Note to s. 464A(1) inserted by No. 26/2017 s. 21.
Note to s. 464A inserted by No. 25/2014 s. 14.

nodes.text: If a person suspected of having committed an offence is in custody for that offence, an investigating official may, within the reasonable time referred to in subsection (1)—
inform the person of the circumstances of that offence; and
question the person or carry out investigations in which the person participates in order to determine the involvement (if any) of the person in that offence.

Before any questioning (other than a request for the person's name and address) or investigation under subsection (2) commences, an investigating official must inform the person in custody that he or she does not have to say or do anything but that anything the person does say or do may be given in evidence.
In determining what constitutes a reasonable time for the purposes of subsection (1) the following matters may be considered—
the period of time reasonably required to bring the person before a bail justice or the Magistrates' Court;
the number and complexity of offences to be investigated;
any need of the investigating official to read and collate relevant material or to take any other steps that are reasonably necessary by way of preparation for the questioning or investigation;
any need to transport the person from the place of apprehension to a place where facilities are available to conduct an interview or investigation;
the number of other people who need to be questioned during the period of custody in respect of the offence for which the person is in custody;
any need to visit the place where the offence is believed to have been committed or any other place reasonably connected with the investigation of the offence;
any time taken to communicate with a legal practitioner, friend, relative, parent, guardian or independent person;
any time taken by a legal practitioner, interpreter, parent, guardian or independent person to arrive at the place where questioning or investigation is to take place;
any time during which the questioning or investigation of the person is suspended or delayed to allow the person to receive medical attention;
any time during which the questioning or investigation of the person is suspended or delayed to allow the person to rest;
the total period of time during which the person has been in the company of an investigating official before and after the commencement of custody;
any other matters reasonably connected with the investigation of the offence.
Section 78D of the Corrections Act 1986 provides for the application of section 464A in relation to persons detained under that Act.

nodes.heading: Questioning or investigation of person already held for another matter

nodes.text: An investigating official may apply to the Magistrates' Court or, if the application is in respect of a child, the Children's Court for an order that a person—

history.raw: S. 464B(1) (a)(iii) substituted by No. 26/2014 s. 455(Sch. item 7.3), amended by No. 39/2022 s. 814.
S. 464B(1) (a)(iv) repealed by No. 26/2014 s. 455(Sch. item 7.3).

nodes.text: who is—
held in a prison or police gaol; or
a forensic resident or a security resident within the meaning of the Disability Act 2006; or
a forensic patient or a security patient within the meaning of the Mental Health and Wellbeing Act 2022; and

reasonably suspected of having committed an offence (being, in the case of an application in respect of a child, an indictable offence), whether in Victoria or elsewhere, other than the offence for which he or she is being held—
be delivered into the custody of the investigating official for the purpose of questioning or investigation in respect of the first-mentioned offence.
An application under subsection (1) must—
be in writing; and
state the grounds on which the application is made; and
be served on the person who is the subject of the application by delivering a true copy of the application—
to the person personally; or
to the person in charge of the place where the person is being held or detained.

At any time after the filing of an application under subsection (1), the Magistrates' Court or Children's Court (as the case may be) may order that the person who is the subject of the application be brought before the court for the hearing of the application under subsection (1).
While an order made under subsection (3) is being carried out, the person is to be taken to be in the legal custody of the person acting under the order.

The Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) must not hear or determine an application under subsection (1) unless the person who is the subject of the application is before the Court.

If the person who is the subject of an application under subsection (1) is not legally represented in a proceeding on the application, the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be)—

must adjourn the hearing of the proceeding to enable the person to obtain legal representation unless satisfied that the person has had, or has refused to have, legal advice provided to him or her in relation to the application; and

must not resume the hearing unless the person is legally represented or the Court is satisfied that he or she has had, or has refused to have, legal advice provided to him or her in relation to the application.

The Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) may order Victoria Legal Aid to provide legal assistance (of a kind to which section 26(1) of the Legal Aid Act 1978 applies) to the person who is the subject of an application under subsection (1) and, despite anything to the contrary in that Act, Victoria Legal Aid must provide legal assistance in accordance with the order.

On an application under subsection (1), the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) may, if satisfied that it is in the interests of justice to do so but subject to subsection (5C), order the transfer of the custody of the person who is the subject of the application to the applicant for the purpose of questioning or investigation for a maximum period of time specified in the order, being a reasonable period within which the questioning or investigation may take place.

history.raw: S. 464B(5) amended by Nos 56/1989 s. 286(Sch. 2 item 7.7), 57/1989 s. 5(1)(b)(ii), substituted by No. 86/2000 s. 4(4).

nodes.text: In determining what constitutes a reasonable period for the purposes of an order under subsection (5), the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) must have regard to—
the matters specified in section 464A(4), with any necessary modifications; and
if the person is a child, his or her age.

The Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be), on making an order under subsection (5), may make any further order that it thinks fit as to where, and the circumstances under which, the questioning or investigation may take place but it must not order that the questioning or investigation take place somewhere other than the place at which the person who is the subject of the order was held or detained at the time of the application for the order under subsection (5) unless it is not practicable for the questioning or investigation to take place there.
The Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) must not make an order under subsection (5) in respect of a person referred to in subsection (1)(a)(ii) or (iii) unless—

history.raw: S. 464B(5C) inserted by No. 86/2000 s. 4(4), amended by No. 29/2020 s. 9(1).

nodes.text: having considered any known likely psychological effect of the questioning on the person; and
having received evidence (whether oral or written) on the fitness of the person to be questioned given by a medical practitioner—
it is satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the person is fit to be questioned.

A person is unfit to be questioned for the purposes of subsection (5C) if, because the person's mental processes are disordered or impaired, the person is or, at some time during the questioning, will be—
unable to understand the nature of the questioning (namely that it is questioning to ascertain his or her involvement in the commission of an offence); or
unable to follow the course of questioning; or
unable to give instructions to his or her legal practitioner; or
unable to understand that he or she does not have to say or do anything but that anything he or she does say or do may be given in evidence.
On making an order under subsection (5) in respect of a person referred to in subsection

history.raw: S. 464B(5E) inserted by No. 86/2000 s. 4(4), amended by No. 29/2020 s. 9(1).

nodes.text: (a)(ii) or (iii), the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be)—
must include in that order a condition that—
subject to subsection (5F), an independent person is to be present while any questioning or investigation takes place in accordance with the order; and

before the commencement of any questioning or investigation, the investigating official must allow the person to communicate with the independent person in circumstances in which as far as practicable the communication will not be overheard; and
may include in that order any other condition that it thinks fit in the interests of the well-being of the person during any questioning or investigation.

The Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) is not required to include in an order under subsection (5) a condition referred to in subsection (5E)(a)(i) if the person who is the subject of the order applies to the Court for that condition not to be included and the Court is satisfied that, in all the circumstances, it is appropriate not to include it.
On making an order under subsection (5), the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) must inform the person who is the subject of the order—
that he or she does not have to say or do anything but that anything he or she does say or do may be given in evidence; and
that the investigating official must give him or her the information required to be given by subsection (6) and section 464C(1); and

if the person was held in a prison or police gaol at the time of the application, that the making of the order does not prevent a senior police officer from authorising the conduct of a non-intimate compulsory procedure on the person under section 464SA.
An audiovisual recording must be made of the following—

history.raw: S. 464B(5H) inserted by No. 86/2000 s. 4(4), amended by No. 27/2006 s. 17(2).

nodes.text: the giving of any information required to be given by subsection (6) and section 464C(1);
any response of the person in custody to the giving of that information;
any questioning that takes place in accordance with an order made under subsection (5) and anything said by the person questioned.

If an order is made under subsection (5), before any questioning or investigation commences, an investigating official must inform the person who is the subject of the order that he or she does not have to say or do anything but that anything the person does say or do may be given in evidence.

An order under subsection (5) has effect as a suspension of a direction in a warrant of commitment to deliver a person to the place of detention specified in the warrant or to hold a person in that place (as the case may be).
The Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) may, subject to subsection (8A)—
extend a period of custody ordered under subsection (5); or
on a subsequent application under subsection (1), make orders whether in respect of the same or a different offence reasonably suspected of having been committed by the person.

The Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) must not extend a period of custody ordered under subsection (5) or, on a subsequent application under subsection (1), make an order against the same person in respect of the same offence unless satisfied that there is a reasonable prospect that further questioning or investigation will assist in determining the involvement (if any) of the person in the commission of the offence.
In determining the length of any extension of a period of custody ordered under subsection (5), the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) must have regard to—
the matters specified in section 464A(4), with any necessary modifications; and
if the person is a child, his or her age.
At—
the end of the period, or any extended period, specified in an order under subsection (5); or
the cessation of questioning or investigation—

whichever is the earlier, the investigating official must deliver the person who is the subject of the order to the place of detention at which the person was held or detained at the time of the application for the order.
The making of an order under subsection (5) does not prevent a senior police officer from giving an authorisation under section 464SA.
In this section—

history.raw: S. 464B(10) inserted by No. 86/2000 s. 4(9), amended by No. 72/2004 s. 26(a)(b).

nodes.heading: child
nodes.text: , in relation to a person suspected of having committed an offence, means a person who is under 18 years of age at the time of the suspected commission of the offence but does not include any person who is 19 years of age or over when—

history.raw: S. 464B(10) def. of child amended by No. 72/2013 s. 4(2)(a), substituted by No. 32/2024 s. 804.

nodes.text: an application is made under this section in respect of the person; or
the person gives informed consent under this section;
It is conclusively presumed that a child who is under 12 years of age cannot commit an offence—see section 10 of the Youth Justice Act 2024.

history.raw: Note to s. 464B inserted by No. 25/2014 s. 15.

nodes.heading: investigating official
nodes.text: , in relation to an offence committed outside Victoria, includes a person (other than a person who is engaged in covert investigations under the orders of a superior) who is—

history.raw: S. 464B(10) def. of investigating official inserted by No. 72/2013 s. 4(2)(b).

nodes.text: a member of—
the Australian Federal Police; or
the police force of another State or a Territory; or

a person appointed by or under an Act of the Commonwealth or another State or a Territory whose functions or duties include functions or duties in respect of the prevention or investigation of offences;
Part IC of the Crimes Act 1914 of the Commonwealth applies if the investigating official is a member of the Australian Federal Police.

nodes.heading: offence
nodes.text: includes an offence against a law of the Commonwealth or another State or a Territory.

history.raw: S. 464B(10) def. of offence inserted by No. 72/2013 s. 4(2)(b).

nodes.text: An investigating official may question a person (other than a child) who is held in a prison or police gaol and is reasonably suspected of having committed an offence (whether in Victoria or elsewhere) other than the offence for which he or she is being held about his or her involvement (if any) in that offence if—
the investigating official is satisfied that the person is not incapable of giving informed consent by reason of mental impairment; and
the person gives informed consent in accordance with subsection (13).
Section 41 of the Corrections Act 1986 provides for visits by the police to prisoners, which may include questioning to which this section does not apply.
A person must not be removed from the prison or police gaol in which he or she is being held for the purpose of questioning under subsection (11) unless subsection (16) applies.

history.raw: S. 464B(12) inserted by No. 72/2013 s. 4(3), amended by No. 29/2020 s. 9(2).

nodes.text: Questioning or investigations involving removal from prison or police gaol may be authorised by a court order under subsection (5).

A person gives informed consent to be questioned if the person consents after an investigating official informs the person, in language likely to be understood by the person, of the following matters—
the nature of the offence which the person is suspected of having committed;
that the person may refuse to be questioned;
that if the person gives consent, he or she does not have to say or do anything but that anything the person does say or do may be given in evidence;

that if the person gives consent, he or she may withdraw that consent at any time before the questioning is completed but anything the person says or does before withdrawal of consent may be given in evidence;
that if the person refuses to be questioned, an application may be made to the Magistrates' Court for an order under this section;
that if the Magistrates' Court makes an order under this section, the person may be delivered into the custody of the investigating official for the purpose of questioning;
the person's rights under sections 464C, 464D and 464F, unless Part IC of the Crimes Act 1914 of the Commonwealth applies.
A person may exercise any applicable right under section 464C, 464D or 464F before deciding whether or not to consent to be questioned.
An audiovisual recording must be made of—
the giving of the information referred to in subsection (13); and
any response of the person in custody to the giving of that information; and
any questioning of the person that takes place and anything said by the person questioned; and
any withdrawal of consent to the questioning.
An investigating official may remove a person being held in a police gaol for the purpose of questioning under subsection (11) if—
the police gaol is located in the same building as a police station; and
the person is to be removed to a room in the police station; and
the person is not to be taken outside the building; and
the person consents to being removed to a room in the police station; and
the officer in charge of the police gaol gives approval under subsection (17).
An officer in charge of a police gaol may approve the removal of a person to a room in a police station under subsection (16) if satisfied that the use of the room—
is in the best interests of the person to be questioned, having regard to privacy and confidentiality; or
enables an audiovisual recording required by subsection (15) to be made; or
for any other reason is preferable to conducting the questioning in the police gaol.
A person removed under subsection (16) from a police gaol to a room in a police station is in the custody of the investigating official.
The removal of a person from a police gaol to another part of the same building under subsection
has effect as a suspension of a direction in a warrant of commitment to deliver the person to the place of detention specified in the warrant or to hold the person in that place.
At the cessation of questioning, the investigating official must deliver the person to the police gaol from which the person was removed.
Section 78D of the Corrections Act 1986 provides for the application of section 464B in relation to persons detained under that Act.

nodes.heading: Right to communicate with friend, relative and legal practitioner

nodes.text: Before any questioning or investigation under section 464A(2) commences, an investigating official must inform the person in custody that he or she—
may communicate with or attempt to communicate with a friend or relative to inform that person of his or her whereabouts; and
may communicate with or attempt to communicate with a legal practitioner (whether the term legal practitioner or lawyer is used)—
and, unless the investigating official believes on reasonable grounds that—
the communication would result in the escape of an accomplice or the fabrication or destruction of evidence; or
the questioning or investigation is so urgent, having regard to the safety of other people, that it should not be delayed—
the investigating official must defer the questioning and investigation for a time that is reasonable in the circumstances to enable the person to make, or attempt to make, the communication.
Subject to subsection (1), if a person wishes to communicate with a friend, relative or legal practitioner, the investigating official in whose custody the person then is—
must afford the person reasonable facilities as soon as practicable to enable the person to do so; and

must allow the person's legal practitioner or a clerk of the legal practitioner to communicate with the person in custody in circumstances in which as far as practicable the communication will not be overheard.

This section also applies to any questioning or investigation in accordance with an order made under section 464B(5) or any questioning conducted by consent under section 464B(11), unless Part IC of the Crimes Act 1914 of the Commonwealth applies.
This section does not apply to questioning or investigation in connection with an offence under section 49(1) of the Road Safety Act 1986.

If a person in custody does not have a knowledge of the English language that is sufficient to enable the person to understand the questioning, an investigating official must, before any questioning or investigation under section 464A(2) commences, arrange for the presence of a competent interpreter and defer the questioning or investigation until the interpreter is present.

This section also applies to any questioning or investigation in accordance with an order made under section 464B(5) or any questioning conducted by consent under section 464B(11), unless Part IC of the Crimes Act 1914 of the Commonwealth applies.
This section does not apply to questioning or investigation in connection with an offence under section 49(1) of the Road Safety Act 1986.
If a person in custody is under the age of 18 years, an investigating official must not, subject to subsection (2), question or carry out an investigation under section 464A(2) unless—
a parent or guardian of the person in custody or, if a parent or guardian is not available, an independent person is present; and

before the commencement of any questioning or investigation, the investigating official has allowed the person in custody to communicate with his or her parent or guardian or the independent person in circumstances in which as far as practicable the communication will not be overheard.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the investigating official believes on reasonable grounds that—
the communication necessary to give effect to subsection (1)(a) would result in the escape of an accomplice or the fabrication or destruction of evidence; or
the questioning or investigation is so urgent, having regard to the safety of other people, that it should not be delayed.
This section also applies to any questioning or investigation in accordance with an order made under section 464B(5).
This section does not apply to questioning or investigation in connection with an offence under section 49(1) of the Road Safety Act 1986.

nodes.heading: Right of foreign national to communicate with consular office

nodes.text: If a person in custody is not a citizen or permanent resident of Australia, the investigating official in whose custody the person then is must, before any questioning or investigation under section 464A(2) commences, inform the person in custody that he or she may communicate with or attempt to communicate with the consular office of the country of which the person is a citizen and, unless the investigating official believes on reasonable grounds that—
the communication would result in the escape of an accomplice or the fabrication or destruction of evidence; or
the questioning or investigation is so urgent, having regard to the safety of other people, that it should not be delayed—
the investigating official must defer the questioning or investigation for a time that is reasonable in the circumstances to enable the person to make, or attempt to make, the communication.

Subject to subsection (1), if a person referred to in that subsection wishes to communicate with the consular office of the country of which he or she is a citizen, the investigating official in whose custody the person then is must afford the person reasonable facilities as soon as practicable to enable the person to do so.

This section also applies to any questioning or investigation in accordance with an order made under section 464B(5) or any questioning conducted by consent under section 464B(11), unless Part IC of the Crimes Act 1914 of the Commonwealth applies.
This section does not apply to questioning or investigation in connection with an offence under section 49(1) of the Road Safety Act 1986.

nodes.heading: Victorian Aboriginal Legal Service to be notified if Aboriginal person or Torres Strait Islander taken into custody

nodes.text: An investigating official must notify VALS if—
a person is taken into custody; and
either—
the person states (whether or not in response to a question asked by an investigating official) that they are an Aboriginal person or a Torres Strait Islander; or
the investigating official who took the person into custody knows or is of the opinion that the person is an Aboriginal person or a Torres Strait Islander.
Section 464AAB requires that an investigating official who takes a person into custody must ask the person whether they are an Aboriginal person or a Torres Strait Islander.
The notification must be made—
within one hour of the person being taken into custody; or
if it is not practicable to do so within one hour, as soon as it is practicable to do so.
As soon as practicable after VALS is notified, an investigating official must inform the person taken into custody of that notification.
In this section—

nodes.heading: VALS
nodes.text: means the Victorian Aboriginal Legal Service Co-operative Ltd (ABN 45 926 675 900).

nodes.heading: Recording of information required to be given to person in custody

history.raw: S. 464G inserted by No. 37/1988 s. 5, amended by No. 86/2000 s. 8(1) (ILA s. 39B(1)).

nodes.text: If a person is in custody in relation to an indictable offence, an investigating official who is required by sections 464A(3), 464C(1) and 464F(1) to give the person in custody certain information must record (by audio recording or audiovisual recording), if practicable, the giving of that information and the person's responses, if any.
Subsection (1) is subject to section 464B(5H) and (15).

history.raw: S. 464G(2) inserted by No. 86/2000 s. 8(1), amended by No. 72/2013 s. 8.

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (2), evidence of a confession or admission made to an investigating official by a person who—
was suspected; or
ought reasonably to have been suspected—
of having committed an offence is inadmissible as evidence against the person in proceedings for an indictable offence unless—

if the confession or admission was made before the commencement of questioning, the confession or admission was recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording, or the substance of the confession or admission was confirmed by the person and the confirmation was recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording; or

if the confession or admission was made during questioning at a place where facilities were available to conduct an interview, the questioning and anything said by the person questioned was recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording; or

if the confession or admission was made during questioning at a place where facilities were not available to conduct an interview, the questioning and anything said by the person questioned was recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording, or the substance of the confession or admission was confirmed by the person questioned and the confirmation was recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording; or

if the confession or admission was made during questioning in accordance with an order made under section 464B(5), the questioning and anything said by the person was recorded by audiovisual recording—

history.raw: S. 464H(1)(f) inserted by No. 86/2000 s. 6(1)(b), amended by No. 27/2006 s. 17(6)(b).

nodes.text: and, if either an audio recording or an audiovisual recording was made, that recording or, if both an audio recording and an audiovisual recording were made, the audiovisual recording is available to be tendered in evidence.

A court may admit evidence of a confession or admission otherwise inadmissible by reason of subsection (1) if the person seeking to adduce the evidence satisfies the court on the balance of probabilities that the circumstances—
are exceptional; and
justify the reception of the evidence.

If the questioning or confession or admission, or the confirmation of a confession or admission, of a person is recorded as required under this section or the giving of information is recorded as required under section 464B(5H) or 464G, the investigating official must give to the person or his or her legal practitioner without charge—
if either an audio recording or an audiovisual recording was made, a copy of that recording as soon as practicable but not later than 7 days after the recording was made; and
if both an audio recording and an audiovisual recording were made—
the audio recording as soon as practicable but not later than 7 days after the recording was made; and
if the person is charged with an offence to which the recording relates, a copy of the audiovisual recording as soon as practicable but not later than 7 days after the person is charged; and
if a transcript of the recording is prepared, a copy of the transcript as soon as practicable but not later than 7 days after the transcript was made.

On request by a person charged with an offence or the legal practitioner representing that person, the investigating official must provide an additional copy of the audiovisual recording referred to in subsection (3).
Nothing in this section prevents the use of an audio recording or audiovisual recording in a proceeding for a summary offence.

nodes.heading: No power to detain person not under arrest
nodes.text: Nothing in sections 464 to 464H (except as provided by an order made under section 464B(5)) confers a power to detain against his or her will a person who is not under arrest.

history.raw: S. 464I inserted by No. 37/1988 s. 5, amended by No. 86/2000 s. 8(2).

nodes.heading: Right to remain silent etc. not affected
nodes.text: Nothing in this subdivision affects—

history.raw: S. 464J inserted by No. 37/1988 s. 5, amended by No. 84/1989 s. 6.

nodes.text: the right of a person suspected of having committed an offence to refuse to answer questions or to participate in investigations except where required to do so by or under an Act or a Commonwealth Act; or
the onus on the prosecution to establish the voluntariness of an admission or confession made by a person suspected of having committed an offence; or
the onus on the prosecution to prove that an admission or confession was made in such circumstances as to make it unlikely that the truth of the admission or confession was adversely affected; or
the discretion of a court to exclude unfairly obtained evidence; or
the discretion of a court to exclude illegally or improperly obtained evidence.
In this section—

nodes.heading: authorised person
nodes.text: means—

history.raw: S. 464JA(1) def. of authorised person amended by Nos 64/2010 s. 3(1), 43/2012 s. 3(Sch. item 11.2), 82/2012 s. 159(1), 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.19(a)), 31/2024 s. 113(Sch. 1 item 7).

nodes.text: a member of Victoria Police personnel (other than a protective services officer);
a person or body engaged to provide services to Victoria Police in relation to the installation or maintenance of recording equipment;
the Director of Public Prosecutions for Victoria or a person acting under the authority of the Director;

history.raw: S. 464JA(3)(c) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.19(b)).

nodes.text: the Chief Crown Prosecutor or a Crown Prosecutor or Associate Crown Prosecutor appointed under the Public Prosecutions Act 1994;
a person employed in the Office of Public Prosecutions under the Public Prosecutions Act 1994;
a legal practitioner representing—
the State; or
an informant;
a legal practitioner representing—
a suspect recorded under section 464B(5H), 464G or 464H; or
a co-accused of the suspect;
an officer or employee of Victoria Legal Aid employed under the Legal Aid Act 1978;
a court or a person acting under the direction of a court;
a coroner within the meaning of the Coroners Act 2008 or a person acting under the direction of a coroner;
the Commissioner for Law Enforcement Data Security appointed under Part 2 of the Commissioner for Law Enforcement Data Security Act 2005 or a person acting under his or her direction;
the Chief Examiner or an Examiner appointed under Part 3 of the Major Crime (Investigative Powers) Act 2004 or a person acting under the direction of the Chief Examiner or an Examiner;
the Commissioner within the meaning of the Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission Act 2011 or a person acting under his or her direction;
the Chief Integrity Inspector within the meaning of the Integrity Oversight Victoria Act 2011 or a person acting under his or her direction;
a member of the Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council or a person acting under his or her direction;
a person, or person belonging to a class of persons, prescribed for the purposes of this definition;
an investigating official or person acting under his or her direction;
a person engaged by a Department or agency to store or retrieve a record;

nodes.heading: publish
nodes.text: means—
insert in a newspaper or other publication; or
disseminate by broadcast, telecast or cinematograph; or
bring to the notice of the public or any member of the public by any other means, including by publication on the Internet;

nodes.heading: recording
nodes.text: means a recording made in accordance with section 464B(5H), 464G or 464H.
A person must not knowingly possess an audio recording or an audiovisual recording unless the person—
is the suspect; or
is a legal practitioner representing the suspect; or
is an authorised person acting in the performance of his or her duties; or

has possession of the recording in a sealed package in the course of his or her duties as a person engaged by a person referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c) to transport the recording to that person.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum).
The maximum fine that may be imposed on a body corporate found guilty of an offence against this subsection is 600 penalty units: see section 113D of the Sentencing Act 1991.
A person must not play an audio recording or an audiovisual recording to another person unless—
the recording is played for purposes connected with any civil or criminal proceeding and any inquiry before any court or tribunal; or
the recording is played for purposes connected with an investigation of a death or a fire or an inquest held by a coroner; or
the recording is played for purposes connected with disciplinary action against a police officer under the Victoria Police Act 2013; or
the recording is played for purposes connected with disciplinary action against a legal practitioner; or
the recording is played in accordance with the direction of a court under section 464JB; or
the recording is played in accordance with section 464JD; or
the recording is played by an authorised person acting in the course of his or her duties.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum).
The maximum fine that may be imposed on a body corporate found guilty of an offence against this subsection is 600 penalty units: see section 113D of the Sentencing Act 1991.
A person must not supply or offer to supply an audio recording or an audiovisual recording to another person other than—
the suspect in relation to whom the recording was made;
a legal practitioner representing the suspect;
an authorised person acting in the performance of his or her duties;
a person engaged by a person referred to in paragraph (a), (b) or (c) to transport the recording.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum).
The maximum fine that may be imposed on a body corporate found guilty of an offence against this subsection is 600 penalty units: see section 113D of the Sentencing Act 1991.

A person, other than an authorised person acting in the performance of his or her duties, must not copy the whole or any part of an audio recording or an audiovisual recording or permit another person to make such a copy, unless the person is acting in accordance with the direction of a court under section 464JB.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum).
The maximum fine that may be imposed on a body corporate found guilty of an offence against this subsection is 600 penalty units: see section 113D of the Sentencing Act 1991.

An authorised person must not knowingly or recklessly tamper with, modify or erase (in whole or in part) a recording while the recording is being retained under section 464JC, except in accordance with the direction of a court under section 464JB.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum).
The maximum fine that may be imposed on a body corporate found guilty of an offence against this subsection is 600 penalty units: see section 113D of the Sentencing Act 1991.
A person must not publish or cause to be published the whole or any part of an audio recording or an audiovisual recording except in accordance with the direction of a court under section 464JB.
Penalty: Level 7 imprisonment (2 years maximum).
The maximum fine that may be imposed on a body corporate found guilty of an offence against this subsection is 1200 penalty units: see section 113D of the Sentencing Act 1991.
An offence against a provision of this section is a summary offence.

nodes.heading: Court may give directions in relation to a recording

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: recording
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in section 464JA.
A court may give directions, with or without conditions, as to the supply, copying, editing, erasure, playing or publishing of an audio recording or an audiovisual recording.
In this section—

nodes.heading: authorised person
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in section 464JA;

nodes.heading: court
nodes.text: means—
if a criminal proceeding to which the recording relates has commenced but has not been completed, the court hearing the proceeding;
in any other case, the Magistrates' Court;

nodes.heading: Department Head
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in the Public Administration Act 2004;

history.raw: S. 464JC(1) def. of Department Head inserted by No. 64/2010 s. 4(1).

nodes.heading: recording
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in section 464JA.
The Chief Commissioner of Police must keep a copy of a recording, if the recording has been made by a police officer in the course of an investigation, in safe custody.

If the recording has been made by an investigating official who is not a police officer, the recording must be kept in the custody of the Department Head for the Department, where the investigating official made the recording in the course of carrying out duties for or on behalf of that Department.

history.raw: S. 464JC(2A) inserted by No. 64/2010 s. 4(4), amended by Nos 48/2012 s. 47, 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.20).

nodes.text: A recording referred to in subsection (2) or (2A) must be kept for a period of 7 years from the making of the recording.

If the court is satisfied that there is good cause to keep a copy of a recording for a period longer than 7 years, the court may order that the Chief Commissioner of Police or the Department Head retain the copy for a further period specified in the order.
An application for an order under subsection (3) may be made by—
the suspect in relation to whom the recording was made; or
an authorised person acting in the performance of his or her duties.
The court must not make an order under subsection (3) unless—
the court is satisfied that the applicant has given reasonable notice of the application to the suspect and the Chief Commissioner of Police or the Department Head; and
the court has given the suspect and the Chief Commissioner of Police or the Department Head a reasonable opportunity to be heard.

nodes.heading: Use of recordings for training, teaching or testing purposes

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: prescribed person
nodes.text: means—

history.raw: S. 464JD(1) def. of prescribed person amended by Nos 64/2010 s. 5(1), 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.21).

nodes.text: a member of Victoria Police personnel (other than a protective services officer);
a person or body engaged to provide services to Victoria Police in relation to the installation or maintenance of recording equipment;
a legal practitioner or a person training to become a legal practitioner;
a person, or a person belonging to a class of persons, prescribed for the purposes of this section;
an investigating official or a person acting under his or her direction;

nodes.heading: recording
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in section 464JA.
Subject to section 464JA, a recording may be played to a prescribed person for the purposes of training or teaching that person or testing the recording equipment if—
the suspect has been convicted or found guilty of the charge to which the recording relates; and
all legal proceedings in relation to the subject matter in the recording have been concluded; and
all reasonable measures have been taken to prevent the identification of the suspect or any other person (including an alleged victim) from the recording when it is played.

nodes.heading: Fingerprinting
nodes.text: Fingerprinting

nodes.heading: Fingerprinting of adults and children aged 15 or above

history.raw: S. 464K inserted by No. 38/1988 s. 4, amended by Nos 25/1989 s. 11(c), 57/1989 s. 5(1)(c), substituted by No. 129/1993 s. 7.

nodes.text: A police officer may take, or cause to be taken by an authorised person, the fingerprints of a person of or above the age of 15 years who—

history.raw: S. 464K(1) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.22(a)).

nodes.text: is believed on reasonable grounds to have committed; or
has been charged with; or
has been summonsed to answer to a charge for—
an indictable offence or a summary offence referred to in Schedule 7.
A police officer intending to fingerprint a person under this section must inform the person in language likely to be understood by him or her—

history.raw: S. 464K(2) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.22(a)).

nodes.text: of the purpose for which the fingerprints are required; and
of the offence which the person is believed to have committed or with which the person has been charged or for which the person has been summonsed to answer to a charge; and
that the fingerprints may be used in evidence in court; and
that if the person refuses to give his or her fingerprints voluntarily, a police officer may use reasonable force to obtain them; and

history.raw: S. 464K(2)(d) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.22(a)).

nodes.text: that if the person is not charged with a relevant offence within 6 months or is so charged but the charge is not proceeded with or the person is not found guilty of the offence or any other relevant offence before the end of that period, the fingerprints will be destroyed; and
that if the person is or has been fingerprinted under this Subdivision on another occasion, section 464O(3A) may apply to the collective destruction of the person's fingerprints; and
that the fingerprints may not be destroyed if the person dies before the fingerprints are required to be destroyed; and
that the fingerprints may be used for the purposes specified in section 464NB.
Subject to subsection (4), the police officer who informs a person of the matters in subsection (2) must—

history.raw: S. 464K(3) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.22(a)).

nodes.text: record (whether by audio recording or audiovisual recording); or
record in writing signed by the person—
the giving of that information and the person's responses, if any.

If a person is in custody within the meaning of this Subdivision in relation to an indictable offence, the giving of the information under subsection (2) and the person's responses, if any, must be recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording.

If information and a person's responses are recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording in accordance with this section, the police officer giving the information must give or send by post to the person or his or her legal practitioner without charge—
the recording (whether audio recording or audiovisual recording) or a copy of it within 7 days; and
if a transcript of the recording is prepared, a copy of the transcript as soon as practicable.

If information and a person's responses are recorded in writing in accordance with this section, the police officer requesting the person's fingerprints must give to the person, or cause the person to be given, a copy of the signed record forthwith.

history.raw: S. 464K(6) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.22(b)).

nodes.text: A police officer may use reasonable force to take the fingerprints of a person referred to in subsection (1) who refuses to give them voluntarily if the use of reasonable force is authorised by a police officer in charge of a police station at the time of the request or a police officer of or above the rank of sergeant.

history.raw: S. 464K(7) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.22(c)).

nodes.text: If the person from whom fingerprints are required is a child aged 15, 16 or 17 years—

a parent or guardian of the child or, if a parent or guardian cannot be located, an independent person must be present during the request for the fingerprints, the giving of the information referred to in subsection (2) and the taking of the fingerprints; and
if the use of reasonable force has been authorised in accordance with subsection (7), the taking of the fingerprints must be recorded by audiovisual recording, if practicable, or by audio recording.

nodes.heading: Fingerprinting of children aged 14 or under

history.raw: S. 464L inserted by No. 38/1988 s. 4, amended by No. 23/1991 s. 5(a)(b), substituted by No. 129/1993 s. 7.

nodes.text: A police officer must not do any of the following in respect of a child who was under 12 years of age at the time that the child is alleged to have done any act or made any omission which would constitute an offence if the child had been of the age of criminal responsibility—
request the child to give the child's fingerprints;
take fingerprints from the child;
cause any other person to take fingerprints from the child.
It is conclusively presumed that a child who is under 12 years of age cannot commit an offence—see section 10 of the Youth Justice Act 2024.
be requested to give his or her fingerprints; or
have his or her fingerprints taken.
A police officer may take, or cause to be taken by an authorised person, the fingerprints of a child who is 12 years of age or over but under 15 years of age and who—
is believed on reasonable grounds to have committed; or
has been charged with; or
has been summonsed to answer to a charge for—
an indictable offence or a summary offence referred to in Schedule 7 if—
both the child and a parent or guardian of the child consent; or
where consent is refused or the parent or guardian cannot be located, the Children's Court makes an order under section 464M(5).
A police officer wishing to fingerprint a child referred to in subsection (2) must inform the child and the parent or guardian of the child in language likely to be understood by each of them—

history.raw: S. 464L(3) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.23(a)).

nodes.text: of the purpose for which the fingerprints are required; and
of the offence which the child is believed to have committed or with which the child has been charged or for which the child has been summonsed to answer to a charge; and
that the fingerprints may be used in evidence in court; and
that the child, or the child's parent or guardian, may refuse consent to the child's fingerprints being taken; and
that if consent is refused, an application may be made to the Children's Court for an order directing the child to give the child's fingerprints; and

that if the child is not charged with a relevant offence within 6 months or is so charged but the charge is not proceeded with or the child is not found guilty of the offence or any other relevant offence before the end of that period, the fingerprints will be destroyed; and
that if the child is or has been fingerprinted under this Subdivision on another occasion, section 464O(3A) may apply to the collective destruction of the child's fingerprints; and
that the fingerprints may not be destroyed if the child dies before the fingerprints are required to be destroyed; and
that the fingerprints may be used for the purposes specified in section 464NB.

A parent or guardian of a child must be present during the request for the fingerprints under this section, the giving of the information referred to in subsection (3) and the taking of the fingerprints with consent.
Subject to subsection (6), the police officer who informs a child of the matters in subsection (3) must—

history.raw: S. 464L(5) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.23(a)).

nodes.text: record by audio recording or audiovisual recording; or
record in writing signed by the child and the parent or guardian present—
the giving of that information and the responses, if any, of the child and the parent or guardian.

If a child is in custody within the meaning of this Subdivision in relation to an indictable offence, the giving of the information under subsection (3) and the responses, if any, of the child and the parent or guardian must be recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording.

If information and the responses of the child and parent or guardian are recorded by audio recording or audiovisual recording, the police officer giving the information must give or send by post to the child or the child's legal practitioner without charge—
the recording (whether audio recording or audiovisual recording) or a copy of it within 7 days; and
if a transcript of the recording is prepared, a copy of the transcript as soon as practicable.

If information and the responses of the child and parent or guardian are recorded in writing, the police officer requesting the child's fingerprints must give to the child, or cause the child to be given, a copy of the signed record forthwith.

history.raw: S. 464L(8) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.23(b)).
S. 464M inserted by No. 38/1988 s. 4, amended by Nos 25/1989 s. 14(b), 57/1989 s. 5(1)(d)(e), 23/1991 s. 6(1), substituted by No. 129/1993 s. 7.

nodes.text: If a child referred to in section 464L(2) or the child's parent or guardian refuses to consent to the taking of the child's fingerprints or the parent or guardian cannot be located, a police officer may apply to the Children's Court for an order under subsection (5).
An application under subsection (1)—
must be in writing supported by evidence on oath or by affirmation or by affidavit; and

history.raw: S. 464M(2)(a) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 35.3).

nodes.text: if the child is held in a police gaol or is detained in a youth residential centre, must state that fact.

history.raw: S. 464M(9)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.24).

nodes.text: Notice of an application under subsection (1) must be served on—
a parent or guardian of the child; and
if the child is not in custody within the meaning of this Subdivision, the child.
The court may dispense with the requirement of subsection (3)(a) if satisfied that it is impracticable for the applicant to comply.
The Children's Court may make an order directing a child who is 12 years of age or over but under 15 years of age to give the child's fingerprints if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that—
there are reasonable grounds to believe that the child has committed an indictable offence or a summary offence referred to in Schedule 7; and
in all the circumstances the making of the order is justified.
In considering whether the making of the order is justified, the court must take into account amongst other things—
the seriousness of the circumstances surrounding the commission of the offence; and
the alleged degree of participation by the child in the commission of the offence; and
the age of the child.
A child in respect of whom an application under subsection (1) is made—
is not a party to the application; and
may not call or cross-examine any witnesses; and
may not address the court, other than in respect of any matter referred to in subsection (5)(a) or (b) or subsection (6).
In exercising the right of address under subsection (7)(c), a child may be represented by a legal practitioner or, with the leave of the court, a parent or guardian of the child.

history.raw: S. 464M(8) amended by No. 35/1996 s. 453(Sch. 1 item 16.17).

nodes.text: If the court makes an order under subsection (5)—
a parent or guardian of the child or, if a parent or guardian cannot be located, an independent person must be present during the taking of the child's fingerprints; and
a police officer may use reasonable force to take the fingerprints; and
the taking of the fingerprints must be recorded by audiovisual recording, if practicable, or otherwise by audio recording.
After an order under subsection (5) is executed—
the independent person, if any, who witnessed the taking of the fingerprints must endorse on the order the independent person's name and sign the endorsement; and
the person who took the fingerprints must endorse on the order the name of the person, if any, who made the audiovisual recording of the taking of the fingerprints; and
the person who took the fingerprints must give a copy of the order so endorsed to the child.
The endorsements required by subsection (10) to be made on an order under subsection (5) may be made on a copy of the order transmitted by facsimile machine.
If the Children's Court makes an order under subsection (5), it may issue a warrant authorising the person to whom it is directed—
to break, enter and search, if necessary, any place where the child named or described in the warrant is suspected to be; and
to arrest the child named or described in the warrant; and
to take the child without delay to the nearest accessible police station for fingerprinting.
If the Children's Court makes an order under subsection (5) or issues a warrant under subsection (12), it must—
give reasons for its decision; and
cause a note of the reasons to be entered in the records of the court.
The failure of the court to comply with subsection (13) does not invalidate any order made by it but constitutes non-compliance for the purposes of section 464Q(1)(a).
If a child is apprehended under a warrant issued under subsection (12), the warrant ceases to have effect immediately after the child's fingerprints have been taken.

If the Children's Court makes an order under subsection (5) in respect of a child who is held in a prison, police gaol, youth justice centre or youth residential centre, the court must also order that the officer in charge of the place at which the child is held must take the fingerprints of the child or cause them to be taken and must deliver the fingerprints to the applicant within a period of time specified in the order.

history.raw: S. 464M(16) amended by No. 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 9.3).
S. 464N inserted by No. 38/1988 s. 4, amended by Nos 25/1989 ss 11(d), 12(1)(2), 14(c)(d), 56/1989 s. 286(Sch. 2 items 7.8– 7.10), substituted by No. 129/1993 s. 7.

nodes.text: Fingerprints may be taken by means of a device to obtain a record of the fingerprints (a fingerscan) or by any other means.
If—
fingerprints are to be taken in accordance with a court order; or
reasonable force is to be used to take fingerprints—

a person of the same sex as the person to be fingerprinted must, if practicable, take the fingerprints and a police officer involved in investigating the offence for which the fingerprints are required must not, if practicable, take the fingerprints.
If a person of or above the age of 15 years—
has been charged with an indictable offence or a summary offence referred to in Schedule 7; and
is present in a police station because of the charging or has been remanded in custody in relation to the charge—

history.raw: S. 464NA(4)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.25 (b)(i)).

nodes.text: a police officer may take, or cause to be taken by an authorised person, a fingerscan of the person for the purpose only of identifying the person.
A police officer intending to fingerscan a person under this section must inform the person, in language likely to be understood by the person, that the fingerscan—
is to be taken only for the purpose of identifying the person; and
is inadmissible as evidence.
A police officer may use reasonable force to take the fingerscan of a person referred to in subsection (2) who refuses to allow it to be taken voluntarily if—

history.raw: S. 464NA(4) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.25 (b)(i)).

nodes.text: the use of reasonable force is authorised by a police officer in charge of a police station at the relevant time or a police officer of or above the rank of sergeant; and
before fingerscanning the person, the police officer informs the person, in language likely to be understood by the person, that reasonable force may be used to obtain it.
A person of the same sex as the person to be fingerscanned must, if practicable, take the fingerscan.
A fingerscan taken under this section is inadmissible as evidence in any proceeding.

A fingerscan taken under this section which is not required to be destroyed under section 464O may be recorded on a computerised database and may be accessed, disclosed, communicated or made use of by a person for the performance of official duties if the recording, accessing, disclosing, communicating or making use of fingerscans on that database by that person, or a person belonging to a class of persons, for that purpose is authorised in writing by the Chief Commissioner of Police.

nodes.heading: Other purposes for the use or disclosure of fingerprint information

nodes.text: Fingerprints taken in accordance with this Subdivision and any record, copy or photograph of them may be used by a person authorised in writing by the Chief Commissioner of Police for any of the following purposes—
to identify a deceased person;
to identify a person who has suffered a serious injury;
to identify a deceased person in a coronial inquest or investigation.
