specified in the order to undergo the forensic procedure.
If—

history.raw: S. 464ZF(3) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.34).

nodes.text: at any time before the commencement of section 25 of the Crimes (Amendment) Act 1997, a person has been found guilty by a court of a forensic sample offence (within the meaning of that term as then in force); and

at any time on or after that commencement, that person is serving a term of imprisonment or a period of detention in a prison, police gaol or youth justice centre or as a security patient in a designated mental health service for any offence, whether or not a forensic sample offence—

a police officer may apply to the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case may be) for an order directing the person to undergo a forensic procedure for the taking of a sample from any part of the body and the court may make an order accordingly.
In any application to a court under subsection (2) or (3), the police officer must specify the type of sample (whether intimate or non-intimate) sought to be taken in the forensic procedure.

history.raw: S. 464ZF(4) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.34).

nodes.text: If, on or after the commencement of the Crimes (Amendment) Act 2004, an application under subsection (2) or (3) is made in respect of a person aged 18 years or more—

history.raw: S. 464ZF(5) substituted by No. 41/2004 s. 16, amended by No. 72/2004 s. 31(2).

nodes.text: the application may be made without notice to any person; and
the person is not a party to the application; and
the person may not call or cross-examine any witnesses; and

history.raw: S. 464ZF(8)(c) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 35.11).

nodes.text: the person may not address the court, other than in response to inquiries made by the court under subsection (8)(c).
If, on or after the commencement of the Crimes (Amendment) Act 2004, an application under subsection (2) or (3) is made in respect of a child—
notice of the application must be served on the child and a parent or guardian of the child; and
the child is not a party to the application; and
the child may not call or cross-examine any witnesses; and
the child may not address the court, other than in respect of any matter referred to in subsection (8)(a) or (b) or in response to inquiries made by the court under subsection (8)(c).
In exercising the right of address under subsection
(d), a child may be represented by a legal practitioner, or, with the leave of the court, a parent or guardian of the child.

An order made by a court under subsection (2) or (3) before the appeal period in relation to the conviction for the forensic sample offence has expired or an appeal against conviction (if any) has been finally determined (whichever is the later), must not be executed unless—
that appeal period expires; or
an appeal against conviction (if any) is finally determined and the conviction for the forensic sample offence is upheld—
whichever is the later.

If leave to appeal against a conviction for a forensic sample offence is sought after the expiry of the appeal period in relation to the conviction, an order made by a court under subsection (2) before leave to appeal is sought, if not executed before that leave is sought, must not be executed unless—
leave to appeal against the conviction is refused; or
leave to appeal against the conviction is granted and the appeal is finally determined and the conviction for the forensic sample offence is upheld.

If an order made by a court under subsection (2) has been executed after the expiration of the appeal period in relation to the conviction for the forensic sample offence and leave to appeal against the conviction is granted after the expiry of that period—
any sample and any related material and information taken may be retained by a police officer pending the final determination of the appeal against conviction; and

if, on appeal, the conviction for the forensic sample offence is set aside, the Chief Commissioner of Police must without delay destroy, or cause to be destroyed, any sample taken and any related material and information.
If on appeal a conviction for the forensic sample offence is set aside, an order made by a court under subsection (2) or (3) ceases to have effect.

history.raw: S. 464ZF(7) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 40.36).

nodes.text: A court hearing an application under subsection (2) or (3)—
must take into account the seriousness of the circumstances of the forensic sample offence in determining whether to make the order under subsection (2) or (3); and
must be satisfied that, in all the circumstances, the making of the order is justified; and
may make such inquiries on oath or by affirmation or otherwise as it considers desirable.
If a court makes an order under subsection (2) or (3), it must—
give reasons for its decision and cause a copy of the order and reasons to be served—
if the order directs a person (other than a child) to undergo the forensic procedure, on the person; or
if the order directs a child to undergo the forensic procedure, on the child and a parent or guardian of the child; and
inform the person ordered to undergo the forensic procedure that a police officer may use reasonable force to enable the procedure to be conducted.
A failure of a court to comply with subsection (9) does not invalidate any order made by it but constitutes non-compliance for the purposes of section 464ZE(1)(a).

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: child
nodes.text: means a child who is 12 years of age or over but under 18 years of age;

history.raw: S. 464ZFAAA (1) def. of child amended by No. 32/2024 s. 809(1).

nodes.heading: forensic sample offence
nodes.text: means any indictable offence or any offence specified in Schedule 8, other than an offence heard and determined summarily.

history.raw: S. 464ZFAAA (1) def. of forensic sample offence amended by Nos 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 40.37), 72/2013 s. 10(1).

nodes.text: If a court finds a person not guilty because of mental impairment of—
a forensic sample offence (within the meaning of that term as then in force); or
an offence of conspiracy to commit, incitement to commit or attempting to commit a forensic sample offence—

a police officer, at any time following that finding but not later than 6 months after the final determination of an appeal or the expiration of any appeal period (whichever is the later), may apply to the court for an order directing the person to undergo a forensic procedure for the taking of a sample from any part of the body and the court may make an order accordingly.
In an application under subsection (2), the police officer must specify the type of sample (whether intimate or non-intimate) sought to be taken in the forensic procedure.
Notice of an application under subsection (2)—
must be served on the person in respect of whom the order is sought and, if the person is a child, on a parent or guardian of the child; and
must include a requirement that the person in respect of whom the order is sought attend the hearing of the application in person or by the person's legal practitioner.
In determining whether to make an order under subsection (2), a court—
must take into account the seriousness of the circumstances of the forensic sample offence of which the person has been found not guilty because of mental impairment; and
must be satisfied that, in all the circumstances, the making of the order is justified; and
may make such inquiries on oath or by affirmation or otherwise as it considers desirable.
An application made under subsection (2) must be heard in the presence of the person in respect of whom the order is sought or the person's legal practitioner.
A person in respect of whom an application under subsection (2) is made—
is not a party to the application; and
may not call or cross-examine any witnesses; and
may not address the court other than in response to inquiries made by the court under subsection (5)(c).
In exercising the right of address under subsection (7)(c), a person may be represented by a legal practitioner.

An order under subsection (2) in respect of a person who is not a forensic patient or a forensic resident within the meaning of the Crimes (Mental Impairment and Unfitness to be Tried) Act 1997 must include a direction that the person attend—
at a place; and
within a period (commencing after the expiry of the period referred to in subsection (12) during which the order must not be executed)—
specified in the order to undergo the forensic procedure.
If a court makes an order under subsection (2), it must—
give reasons for its decision and cause a copy of the order and reasons to be served on the person ordered to undergo the forensic procedure; and
inform the person ordered to undergo the forensic procedure that a police officer may use reasonable force to enable the procedure to be conducted.
A failure of a court to comply with subsection
does not invalidate any order made by it but constitutes non-compliance for the purposes of section 464ZE(1)(a).

An order made by a court under subsection (2) before the appeal period in relation to the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment has expired or an appeal against the verdict (if any) has been finally determined (whichever is the later), must not be executed unless—
that appeal period expires; or
the appeal against the verdict is dismissed—
whichever is the later.

If leave to appeal against a verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment in respect of a forensic sample offence is sought after the expiry of the appeal period in relation to the verdict, an order made by a court under subsection (2) before leave to appeal is sought, if not executed before that leave is sought, must not be executed unless—
leave to appeal against the verdict is refused; or
leave to appeal against the verdict is granted but the appeal is dismissed.

If an order made by a court under subsection (2) has been executed after the expiry of the appeal period in relation to the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment in respect of a forensic sample offence and leave to appeal against the verdict is granted after the expiry of that period—

any sample and any related material and information taken may be retained by a police officer but may not be used for any purpose pending the final determination of the appeal against the verdict; and
if, on appeal, the verdict is set aside, the Chief Commissioner of Police must, without delay, destroy or cause to be destroyed any sample taken and any related material and information.
If on appeal a verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment is set aside, an order made by a court under subsection (2) ceases to have effect.

nodes.text: If a senior police officer is satisfied that—

nodes.text: an order under section 464ZF(2) in respect of a person was made—
before the commencement of section 11 of the Crimes (DNA Database) Act 2002; or

the order has not been executed; and
the period referred to in section 464ZF(6) during which the order must not be executed has expired—
the senior police officer may serve on the person a notice in accordance with subsections (2) and (3).
A notice must direct the person to attend at a police station specified in the notice within 28 days after service of the notice to undergo the forensic procedure ordered by the court and must state—
the date on which the order under section 464ZF(2) was made;
the court which made the order;
that the person has not undergone the forensic procedure;
that if the person fails to comply with the notice, application for a warrant to arrest the person may be made without further notice to the person;
that the person may wish to seek legal advice as to the effect of the notice;
the name, rank and telephone number of the senior police officer serving the notice.
A copy of the order under section 464ZF(2) must be attached to and served with the notice.
A notice may be served on a person by—
delivering a true copy of the notice to the person personally; or

leaving a true copy of the notice for the person at the person's last or most usual place of residence or business with a person who apparently resides or works there and who is apparently not less than 16 years of age; or
posting the notice to the person at their last known place of residence or business.

If a notice is served by post in accordance with subsection (4)(c), evidence of service must state the manner of ascertainment of the address to which the notice was posted and the time and place of posting.
If a person does not comply with a notice served under this section, a police officer may apply to a magistrate or a registrar of the Magistrates' Court for a warrant under subsection (7).

nodes.text: If a magistrate or a registrar to whom such an application is made is satisfied by evidence on oath or by affirmation or affidavit that—

nodes.text: a notice was served on a person in accordance with this section; and
the person has not undergone the forensic procedure—
the magistrate or registrar may issue a warrant authorising the person to whom it is directed, if necessary—
to break, enter and search by day or by night any place where the person named in the warrant is suspected to be; and
to arrest the person; and
to detain the person for as long as reasonably permits the conduct of the forensic procedure.
Section 464ZFA(2), (3), (4), (5), (6) and (7) apply to a warrant issued under subsection (7) as if it were a warrant issued under section 464ZFA(1B).

nodes.heading: DNA profile sample from registrable offenders under the Sex Offenders Registration Act 2004

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: initial period
nodes.text: means the period of 3 years commencing on the day on which section 52 of the Sex Offenders Registration Amendment (Miscellaneous) Act 2017 comes into operation;

history.raw: S. 464ZFAB(1) def. of initial period inserted by No. 25/2017 s. 53(1).

nodes.heading: registrable offender
nodes.text: has the same meaning as in section 3 of the Sex Offenders Registration Act 2004.
A police officer may, at any time, direct that a DNA profile sample be taken from a person if, at the time that the direction is given—
the person is a registrable offender; and
the Chief Commissioner of Police does not have a sample from the person that may be retained indefinitely.

A senior police officer may serve, or may cause to be served, a notice on a person referred to in subsection (2) directing the person to attend at a police station specified in the notice to have the DNA profile sample taken within 28 days after service of the notice.
A notice under subsection (3) must—
state that if the person fails to comply with the notice, an application for a warrant to arrest the person may be made without further notice to the person; and
state that the person may wish to seek legal advice as to the effect of the notice; and
state the name, rank and telephone number of the senior police officer serving the notice or causing the notice to be served; and
contain the prescribed information, if any.
A notice under subsection (3) must be served by delivering a true copy of the notice to the person personally.
Section 464ZFAA(6), (7) and (8) apply to a notice served under subsection (3) as if it were a notice served under that section.
If a DNA profile sample is taken from a person under this section, the sample taken and any related material and information may be retained indefinitely.

Subsection (7) does not apply if, on appeal against conviction, the finding of guilt of the registrable offender in respect of an offence is quashed or set aside and, but for that offence, the person would not be a registrable offender.
Subject to subsection (10), a police officer may give a direction under subsection (2) to a registrable offender whose reporting obligations under the Sex Offenders Registration Act 2004—

history.raw: S. 464ZFAB(9) inserted by No. 25/2017 s. 53(2) (as amended by No. 3/2019 s. 80).

nodes.text: have been suspended under Division 6 of Part 3 of that Act; or
have been suspended under section 32(1)(b) of that Act; or
have expired under section 34(1) of that Act—
only if a notice under subsection (3) has been served on the registrable offender.

A registrable offender referred to in subsection (9) may refuse to have a DNA profile sample taken and to attend at a police station in compliance with a notice under subsection (3) if the registrable offender demonstrates to the reasonable satisfaction of the senior police officer referred to in subsection (3)—

if the registrable offender was a registrable offender on the commencement of the initial period, that the registrable offender has been resident in Victoria for not less than 2 years and 6 months in aggregate during the initial period; or

that the registrable offender has been resident in Victoria for a continuous period of 12 months at any time after the expiry of the initial period and was a registrable offender during the whole of that period of 12 months.

A person serving a notice under subsection (3) on a registrable offender referred to in subsection (9) must inform the registrable offender, in a manner likely to be understood by the offender, of the following matters—
that the offender may refuse to comply with the notice;
the grounds on which the offender may refuse to comply;
that the offender may wish to seek legal advice as to the effect of the notice.
A senior police officer referred to in subsection (10) must take into account any information provided by the registrable offender.
Before a registrable offender referred to in subsection (9) has a DNA profile sample taken, a police officer must, in a manner likely to be understood by the offender—
inform the offender of the grounds on which the offender may refuse to have the DNA profile sample taken; and
ask the offender whether the offender wishes to refuse.

If a registrable offender does not have a knowledge of the English language that is sufficient to enable the person to understand the matters referred to in subsection (11) or (13), the person informing the offender must arrange for the presence of a competent interpreter and defer the giving of the information until the interpreter is present.

nodes.heading: Senior police officer authorisation—to take DNA profile sample from certain adults

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: DNA offence
nodes.text: means—
an indictable offence or an offence specified in Schedule 8; or
any offence of conspiracy to commit, incitement to commit or attempting to commit an indictable offence or an offence specified in Schedule 8.
A senior police officer may authorise the taking of a DNA profile sample from a person if—
the person—
is found guilty of a DNA offence; or
is found not guilty of a DNA offence, other than an offence heard and determined summarily, because of mental impairment under the Crimes (Mental Impairment and Unfitness to be Tried) Act 1997; and
it is not more than 6 months after—
the final determination of an appeal against the conviction or the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment (as the case requires); or
the expiration of any appeal period; and
the person is not under the age of 18 years at the time—
the finding of guilt for the DNA offence is made; or
the finding of not guilty for the DNA offence because of mental impairment is made; and
the Chief Commissioner of Police does not have a sample from the person that may be retained indefinitely.

An authorisation given for a sample to be taken from a person referred to in subsection (2)(a)(i) before the appeal period in relation to a conviction for the DNA offence has expired or an appeal against the conviction (if any) has been finally determined (whichever is the later), must not be carried out unless—
the appeal period expires; or
an appeal against conviction (if any) is finally determined and the conviction for the DNA offence is upheld.

An authorisation given for a sample to be taken from a person referred to in subsection (2)(a)(ii) before the appeal period in relation to the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment has expired or an appeal against the verdict (if any) has been finally determined (whichever is the later), must not be carried out unless—
the appeal period expires; or
an appeal against the verdict is dismissed.

If leave to appeal against a verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment in respect of a DNA offence is sought after the expiry of the appeal period in relation to the verdict, an authorisation for a sample to be taken from a person referred to in subsection (2)(a)(ii) before leave to appeal is sought, if not carried out before that leave is sought, must not be carried out unless—
leave to appeal against the verdict is refused; or
leave to appeal against the verdict is granted but the appeal is dismissed.

If leave to appeal against a conviction for a DNA offence is sought after the expiry of the appeal period in relation to the conviction, an authorisation for a sample to be taken from a person referred to in subsection (2)(a)(i) before leave to appeal is sought, if not carried out before that leave is sought, must not be carried out unless—
leave to appeal against the conviction is refused; or
leave to appeal against the conviction is granted and the appeal is finally determined and the conviction for the DNA offence is upheld.

If an authorisation for a sample to be taken from a person referred to in subsection (2)(a) has been carried out after the expiry of the appeal period in relation to the conviction for the DNA offence or the verdict of not guilty for the DNA offence because of mental impairment and leave to appeal against the conviction or the verdict (as the case requires) is granted after the expiry of that period—

any sample and any related material and information taken may be retained by a police officer but must not be used for any purpose pending the final determination of the appeal against the conviction or the verdict; and

if, on appeal, the conviction or the verdict is set aside, the Chief Commissioner of Police must, without delay, destroy or cause to be destroyed any sample taken and any related material and information.

If on appeal a conviction for the DNA offence or the verdict of not guilty for the DNA offence because of mental impairment (as the case requires) is set aside, an authorisation for a sample to be taken from a person in respect of the DNA offence ceases to have effect.
An authorisation given under this section must be in writing signed by the senior police officer giving it.

nodes.heading: Notice to attend—to take DNA profile sample from certain adults

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: relevant person
nodes.text: means a person other than a person who is a detained or protected person.

If a senior police officer authorisation for a DNA profile sample to be taken from a relevant person is given, a notice to attend must be attached to the authorisation and served on the person, that requires the person to attend a police station specified in the notice to have the DNA profile sample taken, within 28 days after the expiry of the period referred to in section 464ZFAC(3) or (4) (as the case requires) or the date of service of the notice (whichever is the later).
A notice under subsection (2) must state—
the date on which the senior police officer authorisation was given; and
the kind of DNA profile sample that is to be taken from the person; and
the name, rank and telephone number of the senior police officer who gave the senior police officer authorisation; and
the Chief Commissioner of Police does not have a sample from the person that may be retained indefinitely; and
that if the person fails to comply with the notice, an application for a warrant to arrest the person may be made without further notice to the person; and
that the person may wish to seek legal advice as to the effect of the notice; and
the name, rank and telephone number of the police officer serving the notice or causing the notice to be served; and
that a police officer may use reasonable force to enable the sample to be taken.
A notice under subsection (2) must be served in accordance with section 464ZFAA(4) and (5).
Section 464ZFAA(6), (7) and (8) apply to a notice served under subsection (2) as if it were a notice served under that section.

If a notice under subsection (2) is not served within the period referred to in section 464ZFAC(2)(b), a police officer may, within 28 days of the expiry of that period, apply to a magistrate or registrar of the Magistrates' Court for a warrant under subsection (7).

On an application referred to in subsection (6) being made a magistrate or a registrar may, if satisfied by evidence on oath or by affidavit that the notice was not served on the relevant person, issue a warrant authorising the person to whom it is directed, if necessary—
to break, enter and search by day or by night any place where the relevant person named in the warrant is suspected to be; and
to arrest the relevant person; and
to detain the relevant person for as long as reasonably permits for the DNA profile sample to be taken.
A magistrate or a registrar must not issue a warrant under subsection (7) unless satisfied by evidence on oath or by affidavit that—
reasonable attempts have been made to serve the notice on the relevant person; and
the DNA profile sample has not been taken from the relevant person.
Section 464ZFA(2), (3), (4), (5), (6) and (7) apply to a warrant issued under subsection (7) as if it were a warrant issued under section 464ZFA(1B).

nodes.heading: Senior police officer may authorise taking a DNA profile sample from certain adults and children who have previously provided a sample

nodes.text: A senior police officer, on request from a police officer, may authorise the taking of a DNA profile sample from a person if the senior police officer is satisfied that—
a sample for the purpose of deriving a DNA profile was previously taken from the person—
in accordance with an order made by a court under section 464T, 464U, 464V, 464ZF or 464ZFAAA; or
in accordance with section 464SC, an authorisation given under section 464SE, a direction given under section 464ZFAB or a senior police officer authorisation; and
a forensic scientist has not derived a DNA profile from the sample taken from the person.

A senior police officer may serve, or may cause to be served, a notice on a person referred to in subsection (1) directing the person to attend at a police station specified in the notice within 28 days after service of the notice to take a DNA profile sample.
A notice under subsection (2) must state—
the date on which the senior police officer authorisation was given; and
the kind of DNA profile sample that is to be taken from the person; and
the name, rank and telephone number of the senior police officer who gave the authorisation; and
that the Chief Commissioner of Police does not have a DNA profile of the person; and
that a DNA profile was not able to be derived by a forensic scientist from the sample given by the person—
in accordance with an order made by a court under section 464T, 464U, 464V, 464ZF or 464ZFAAA; or
in accordance with section 464SC, an authorisation given under section 464SE, a direction given under section 464ZFAB or a senior police officer authorisation; and
that if the person fails to comply with the notice, application for a warrant to arrest the person may be made without further notice to the person; and
that the person may wish to seek legal advice as to the effect of the notice; and
the name, rank and telephone number of the police officer serving the notice or causing the notice to be served; and
that a police officer may use reasonable force to enable the DNA profile sample to be taken.
A notice under subsection (2) must be served by delivering a true copy of the notice to the person personally.
Section 464ZFAA(6), (7) and (8) apply to a notice served under subsection (2) as if it were a notice served under that section.

nodes.heading: Warrants issued for forensic procedures under section 464ZF or 464ZFAAA

history.raw: S. 464ZFA (1)(a) amended by No. 26/2014 s. 455(Sch. item 7.5).
S. 464ZFA (2)(a) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.36 (b)(i)).
S. 464ZFA (2)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.36(b)(ii)).
S. 464ZFA (7)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.36(d)(ii)).

nodes.text: If—

history.raw: S. 464ZFA(1) substituted by No. 27/2006 s. 10(2), amended by No. 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 9.3).

nodes.text: before a court makes an order under section 464ZF(3) directing a person to undergo a forensic procedure, that person has been released from the prison, police gaol, youth justice centre or designated mental health service where he or she was serving a term of imprisonment or a period of detention at the time the application for the order was made; or
a person fails to attend the hearing of an application under section 464ZFAAA(2) for an order directing the person to undergo a forensic procedure—
the court may issue a warrant authorising the person to whom it is directed, if necessary—
to break, enter and search by day or by night any place where the person named in the warrant is suspected to be; and
to arrest the person; and
to bring the person before the court for the hearing of the application; and
if that application is granted, to detain the person for as long as reasonably permits the conduct of the forensic procedure.

If a court makes an order under section 464ZF(2) or 464ZFAAA(2) directing a person to undergo a forensic procedure and the person does not comply with a direction referred to in section 464ZF(2A) or 464ZFAAA(9), as the case may be, a police officer may apply to a magistrate or a registrar of the Magistrates' Court for a warrant under subsection (1B).

If a magistrate or a registrar to whom such an application is made is satisfied by evidence on oath or by affirmation or affidavit that the person has not complied with a direction referred to in section 464ZF(2A) or 464ZFAAA(9), the magistrate or registrar may issue a warrant authorising the person to whom it is directed, if necessary—

history.raw: S. 464ZFA(1B) inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 12(1), amended by Nos 27/2006 s. 10(4), 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 35.10).

nodes.text: to break, enter and search by day or by night any place where the person named in the warrant is suspected to be; and
to arrest the person; and
to detain the person for as long as reasonably permits the conduct of the forensic procedure.
A warrant issued under subsection (1) or (1B) may be directed to—
a named police officer; or
generally all police officers.
A warrant issued under subsection (1) or (1B) directed to a named police officer may be executed by any police officer.
If a court issues a warrant under subsection (1) or a magistrate or registrar issues a warrant under subsection (1B), the court, magistrate or registrar must—
give reasons for the decision; and
cause a note of the reasons to be entered in the records of the court.

A failure of a court, magistrate or registrar to comply with subsection (4) does not invalidate any order made by the court, magistrate or registrar but constitutes non-compliance for the purposes of section 464ZE(1)(a).

If a person is arrested under a warrant issued under subsection (1) or (1B), the warrant ceases to have effect immediately after the procedure is completed or on the expiration of a reasonable time (whichever is the earlier).
A police officer who executes a warrant issued under subsection (1B) must, as soon as practicable after executing the warrant—

history.raw: S. 464ZFA(7) inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 12(3), amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.36(d)(i)).

nodes.text: endorse the warrant to that effect; and
cause to be lodged with a registrar of the Magistrates' Court a report signed by the police officer and containing particulars of—
the date and time at which the person was arrested;
the date and time at which the person was released from custody;
the date, time and place at which the forensic procedure was conducted;
the name and position of the person who conducted the forensic procedure and every other person present;
the type of sample taken;
whether reasonable force was used to enable the forensic procedure to be conducted.

nodes.heading: Retention of information following finding of guilt etc.

history.raw: S. 464ZFB (1)(a) amended by No. 41/2004 s. 17, substituted by No. 72/2013 s. 11(2)(a), amended by No. 3/2019 s. 63(3)(a).
S. 464ZFB (1A)(a) substituted by No. 72/2013 s. 11(3)(a), amended by No. 3/2019 s. 63(4)(a).
S. 464ZFB (2)(c) amended by No. 6/2018 s. 68(Sch. 2 item 35.11).
S. 464ZFB (2A)(b) amended by Nos 14/2006 s. 14(b)(ii), 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 40.39) (as amended by No. 29/2011 s. 3(Sch. 1 item 25.1)).

nodes.text: If—
a DNA profile sample is taken or a forensic procedure is conducted on a person of or above the age of 18 years in accordance with section 464R, 464SA, 464SC, 464SE, 464T(3) or 464V(5); and
a court finds the person guilty, or not guilty because of mental impairment, of—
the indictable offence in respect of which the DNA profile sample was taken or the forensic procedure was conducted; or
any other indictable offence arising out of the same circumstances; or
any other indictable offence in respect of which evidence obtained as a result of the DNA profile sample or the forensic procedure had probative value—
the sample taken and any related material and information may be retained indefinitely.
Subsection (1AA) does not apply if—
on appeal against conviction, the finding of guilt or conviction referred to in subsection (1AA) is set aside; or
on appeal against the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment, the verdict referred to in subsection (1AA) is set aside.
If at any time on or after the commencement of section 26 of the Crimes (Amendment) Act 1997—

a DNA profile sample is taken from a DNA person who is a child in accordance with section 464SC or 464SE or a forensic procedure is conducted on a child in accordance with section 464U(7) or 464V(5); and
a court finds the child guilty of—
the offence in respect of which the DNA profile sample was taken or the forensic procedure was conducted; or
any other offence arising out of the same circumstances; or
any other offence in respect of which evidence obtained as a result of the DNA profile sample or forensic procedure had probative value—

a police officer, at any time after the finding of guilt but not later than 6 months after the final determination of an appeal against conviction or sentence or the expiry of any appeal period in respect of the offence (whichever is the later), may apply to the court referred to in paragraph (b) or to the Children's Court for an order permitting the retention of any sample taken and any related material and information and the court may make an order accordingly.
If—

history.raw: S. 464ZFB(1A) inserted by No. 27/2006 s. 11(2), amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: a DNA profile sample is taken from a DNA person who is a child in accordance with section 464SC or 464SE or a forensic procedure is conducted on a child in accordance with section 464U(7) or 464V(5); and
a court finds the child not guilty because of mental impairment of—
the offence in respect of which the DNA profile sample was taken or the forensic procedure was conducted; or
any other offence arising out of the same circumstances; or
any other offence in respect of which evidence obtained as a result of the DNA profile sample or forensic procedure had probative value—

a police officer, at any time after the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment, but not later than 6 months after the final determination of an appeal against the verdict or the expiry of any appeal period in respect of the verdict (whichever is the later), may apply to the court referred to in paragraph (b) for an order permitting the retention of any sample taken and any related material and information and the court may make an order accordingly.
Subsection (1A) does not apply to an offence heard and determined summarily.

history.raw: S. 464ZFB(1B) inserted by No. 27/2006 s. 11(2), amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 40.38).

nodes.text: A court hearing an application under subsection (1) or (1A)—
must take into account the seriousness of the circumstances of the offence in determining whether to make the order under subsection (1) or (1A), as the case requires; and
must be satisfied that, in all the circumstances, the making of the order is justified; and
may make such inquiries on oath or by affirmation or otherwise as it considers desirable.

An order made under subsection (1) before the expiry of the appeal period in respect of the conviction for the offence or the final determination of an appeal against conviction (whichever is the later)—

history.raw: S. 464ZFB(2A) inserted by No. 16/2002 s. 13(2), amended by No. 14/2006 s. 14(b)(i)(ii).

nodes.text: takes effect on that expiry or final determination; and
has no effect if, on appeal against conviction, the finding of guilt or conviction is set aside.

An order made under subsection (1A) before the expiry of the appeal period in respect of the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment or the final determination of an appeal against the verdict (whichever is later)—
takes effect on that expiry or final determination; and
has no effect if, on appeal, the verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment is set aside.

If a court makes an order under subsection (1) or (1A), it must give reasons for its decision and cause a copy of the order and reasons to be served on the person on whom the forensic procedure was conducted.
A failure of a court to comply with subsection (3) does not invalidate any order made by it but constitutes non-compliance for the purposes of section 464ZE(1)(a).

nodes.heading: Destruction of information following finding of guilt etc.

nodes.text: Subject to section 464ZFD(2), if—
a finding of guilt, a conviction or a verdict of not guilty because of mental impairment referred to in section 464ZFB(1AA) is set aside on appeal; or

the finding of guilt of a registrable offender within the meaning of section 3(1) of the Sex Offenders Registration Act 2004 is quashed or set aside on appeal and, but for that offence, the person would not be a registrable offender; or
a police officer does not make an application under section 464ZFB(1) or (1A) within the period specified by that subsection; or
a court refuses to make an order under section 464ZFB(1) or (1A)—
the Chief Commissioner of Police must without delay destroy, or cause to be destroyed, any sample taken and any related material and information.

If a sample or related material and information is required to be destroyed in accordance with this section, the Chief Commissioner of Police must, if the person on whom the procedure was conducted so requests, within 14 days after receiving the request, notify in writing that person of whether the destruction has occurred.
A person who knowingly—
fails to destroy; or
uses, or causes or permits to be used—

a sample or related material and information required by this section to be destroyed is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

A person who at any time uses, or causes or permits to be used, or otherwise disseminates information derived from, any sample or related material and information required by this section to be destroyed except in good faith for the purposes of section 464ZFD(2) is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).
The Chief Commissioner of Police may keep a DNA database system.

Information (including information which may identify the person from whom a DNA profile sample was taken or on whom a forensic procedure was conducted) obtained from the analysis of samples taken or procedures conducted in accordance with sections 464R to 464ZA, section 464ZF, 464ZFAAA or 464ZFAB, 464ZFAC, 464ZFAE or sections 464ZGB to 464ZGD (as the case may be), and which in accordance with this Subdivision may be retained, may be included in the DNA database system kept under subsection (1AA).

Information (other than information which may identify the person from whom a DNA profile sample was taken or on whom a forensic procedure was conducted) obtained from the analysis of samples taken or procedures conducted in accordance with this Subdivision may be retained and included in the DNA database system kept under subsection (1AA) for statistical purposes.

nodes.heading: Report to Attorney-General
nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police, on or as soon as practicable after 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October of each year, must submit to the Attorney-General a report that contains—
a list that identifies by a unique identifying number every sample taken in accordance with this Subdivision within the period to which the report relates; and
the date on which every sample listed in the report was taken; and

information on whether any of the samples listed in the report or in any previous report submitted under this section have been destroyed within the period to which the report relates and the reason for the destruction of the sample; and
if a sample has been destroyed, the date that the requirement to destroy it arose, the date of destruction and the name of the person who has destroyed it; and

history.raw: S. 464ZFE(d) amended by No. 41/2004 s. 18(a), substituted by No. 3/2019 s. 65(b).

nodes.text: information on any DNA profile sample that has been retained for 12 months or more including the status of any investigation of the DNA person from whom the sample was taken; and

information on forensic material taken from suspects in accordance with section 464R, 464T or 464U that has been retained for 12 months or more including the status of any investigation of the suspect from whom the forensic material was taken; and
the number of authorisations given under sections 464SA and 464SE within the period to which the report relates; and

history.raw: S. 464ZFE(e) inserted by No. 41/2004 s. 18(b), amended by No. 3/2019 s. 65(c).

nodes.text: the number of authorisations refused to be given under sections 464SA and 464SE within the period to which the report relates.

history.raw: S. 464ZFE(f) inserted by No. 41/2004 s. 18(b), amended by No. 3/2019 s. 65(d).
S. 464ZG inserted by No. 84/1989 s. 5, substituted by No. 129/1993 s. 7.

nodes.text: In this section, relevant offence means—
the indictable offence in respect of which the DNA profile sample was taken or the forensic procedure was conducted; or
any other indictable offence arising out of the same circumstances; or
any other indictable offence in respect of which the evidence obtained as a result of the DNA profile sample or the forensic procedure has probative value.
Subject to section 464ZFD(2), if a DNA profile sample has been taken or a forensic procedure has been conducted on a person and—
the person has not been charged with a relevant offence at the end of the period of 12 months after the taking of the sample or the conduct of the procedure; or

the person has been so charged but the charge is not proceeded with or the person is not found guilty (except because of mental impairment) of the offence or any other relevant offence, whether on appeal or otherwise, before the end of that period—
the Chief Commissioner of Police, subject to subsection (5), must destroy, or cause to be destroyed, at the time specified in subsection (4) any sample taken and any related material and information.
A sample and any related material and information referred to in subsection (3) must be destroyed—
in a case to which subsection (3)(a) applies, immediately after that period of 12 months; or
in a case to which subsection (3)(b) applies—
within one month after the conclusion of the proceedings and the end of any appeal period; or
if the proceedings have been adjourned under section 75 of the Sentencing Act 1991, within one month of dismissal under that section.

A police officer may, before the end of a period referred to in subsection (4), apply, without notice to any other person, to the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court (as the case requires) for an order extending that period and, if the court makes such an order, the reference to the period in subsection (4) is a reference to that period as so extended.

history.raw: S. 464ZG(5) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: If the Magistrates' Court or the Children's Court makes an order under subsection (5), it must give reasons for its decision and cause a copy of the order to be served on the person from whom the DNA profile sample was taken or on whom the forensic procedure was conducted.

If a sample or related material and information is required to be destroyed in accordance with this section, the Chief Commissioner of Police must, if the person on whom the procedure was conducted so requests, within 14 days after receiving the request, notify in writing that person of whether the destruction has occurred.
A person who knowingly—
fails to destroy; or
uses, or causes or permits to be used—

a sample or related material and information required by this section to be destroyed is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

A person who at any time uses, or causes or permits to be used, or otherwise disseminates information derived from, any sample or related material and information required by this section to be destroyed except in good faith for the purposes of a relevant offence or for the purposes of section 464ZFD(2) is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).
Subject to section 464ZFD(2), if—

a person has a DNA profile sample taken or undergoes a forensic procedure as a child in accordance with this Subdivision, whether before or after the commencement of section 28 of the Crimes (Amendment) Act 1997; and
any sample taken is not required to be destroyed under this Subdivision, other than under this subsection; and
the person is not found guilty of any further offence before attaining the age of 26 years—
the Chief Commissioner of Police must without delay destroy, or cause to be destroyed, any sample taken and any related material and information.
Subsection (1) does not apply if—
the person from whom the sample was taken is found guilty of—
the offence in relation to which the DNA profile sample was taken or the forensic procedure was conducted; or
an offence arising out of the same circumstances as the offence referred to in subparagraph (i); or
an offence in respect of which evidence obtained as a result of the DNA profile sample or the forensic procedure had probative value; and
the offence of which the person is found guilty is—
an offence against this Act; or
an offence at common law the maximum penalty for which is specified by this Act; and
the offence of which the person is found guilty is punishable by level 4 imprisonment (15 years maximum) or more (however the penalty is described); and
the sample—
was taken in accordance with an order under section 464ZF(2); or
is the subject of an order under section 464ZFB(1).

history.raw: S. 464ZGB (3)(g) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).
S. 464ZGB (3)(h) amended by No. 13/2010 s. 51(Sch. item 17.10).

nodes.text: A person of or above the age of 18 years may volunteer to give a sample (whether an intimate or non-intimate sample) to a police officer.

history.raw: S. 464ZGB(1) amended by Nos 72/2004 s. 32, 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: A sample may only be given under this section if the person volunteering to give it consents in accordance with this section and that consent is not withdrawn prior to the giving of the sample.

A person consents in accordance with this section only if, in the presence of an independent person, he or she consents after a police officer has informed the person in language likely to be understood by the person—

history.raw: S. 464ZGB(3) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: that any sample that is given will be analysed;

that information obtained from the analysis will be placed on a DNA database and may be used for the purpose of a criminal investigation or any other purpose for which the DNA database may be used under this Subdivision or under a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction;
that the person may choose whether the information obtained from analysis of the sample may be used—
only for a limited purpose to be specified by the volunteer; or
for the purpose of a criminal investigation or any other purpose for which the DNA database may be used under this Subdivision or under a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction;
that information obtained from the analysis could produce evidence to be used in a court;
that the person is under no obligation to give a sample;
that if the person consents to give a sample, he or she may at any time before the sample is taken, withdraw that consent;
that the person may consult a legal practitioner (whether the term legal practitioner or lawyer is used) before deciding whether or not to consent to give a sample;
that the person may at any time (including after he or she has been charged with an offence) withdraw his or her consent to the retention of the sample;

that where the person withdraws his or her consent to the retention of the sample, a police officer may nevertheless apply to a court for an order to retain the sample and any related material and information;
that the person may request that the sample be taken by or in the presence of a medical practitioner, nurse, midwife or dentist of his or her choice.
A police officer who informs a person of the matters in subsection (3) must—

history.raw: S. 464ZGB(4) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: record the giving of the information and the person's responses, if any—
in writing signed by both the person and the independent person witnessing the giving of the consent; and
by audiovisual recording, if practicable, or otherwise by audio recording; and
give or send by registered post to the person or his or her legal practitioner, without charge—
a copy of the audiovisual recording or audio recording as soon as practicable, but not more than 7 days after the information is given; and
a copy of the written record, signed by both the person and the independent person, forthwith.

nodes.heading: Withdrawal of consent prior to giving sample

nodes.text: A person, at any time prior to giving a sample, may withdraw the consent that was given by him or her in accordance with section 464ZGB either—

history.raw: S. 464ZGC(1) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: orally; or
in writing—
to a police officer or to the person authorised to take the sample.

If, prior to giving a sample, a person withdraws his or her consent orally, a police officer or the person authorised to take the sample must, as soon as practicable, record in writing the withdrawal of consent.

history.raw: S. 464ZGC(2) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: The procedure to be conducted to take a sample from a person following the giving of consent in accordance with section 464ZGB must—
be in accordance with the procedure set out in section 464Z; and
be recorded by audiovisual recording, if practicable, and if the person consents.
If the taking of a sample voluntarily given by a person is recorded by audiovisual recording, a police officer must—
without charge; and
as soon as practicable but not more than 7 days after the sample was taken—
give or send by registered post a copy of the audiovisual recording to the person who voluntarily gave the sample.

If a person has given his or her consent in accordance with section 464ZGB, and a sample has been taken, that person may at any time after the sample has been taken, by notice in writing to the Chief Commissioner of Police, withdraw his or her consent to the retention of that sample.
Subject to subsection (5) and section 464ZFD(2), if a person has voluntarily given a sample in accordance with sections 464ZGB to 464ZGD and either—
that person in accordance with subsection (1) has withdrawn his or her consent to the retention of that sample; or
a court has made an order under section 464ZGF for the retention of that sample and any related material and information, and—
the person has not been charged with an indictable offence at the end of the period of 12 months after the order of the court; or

the person has been so charged but the charge is not proceeded with, or the person is not found guilty of the indictable offence or any other indictable offence for which the sample and any related material and information had probative value, whether on appeal or otherwise, before the end of that period—
the Chief Commissioner of Police, at the time specified in subsection (3), must destroy, or cause to be destroyed, any sample given and any related material and information.
A sample and any related material and information referred to in subsection (2) must be destroyed—
within 28 days after the receipt of the person's notice of withdrawal of consent under subsection (1); or
in a case to which subsection (2)(b)(i) applies, immediately after that period of 12 months; or
in a case to which subsection (2)(b)(ii) applies—
within one month after the conclusion of the proceedings and the end of any appeal period; or
if the proceedings have been adjourned under section 75 of the Sentencing Act 1991, within one month after dismissal under that section.

The Chief Commissioner of Police is not required to comply with the requirements in subsections (2) and (3) to destroy or cause to be destroyed a sample and any related material and information by reason of the person's withdrawal of consent if the Magistrates' Court makes an order under section 464ZGF for the retention of that sample and any related material and information.

If the Magistrates' Court refuses to make an order under section 464ZGF for the retention of a sample and any related material and information, and a person in accordance with subsection (1) has withdrawn his or her consent to the retention of that sample, the Chief Commissioner of Police must immediately destroy, or cause to be immediately destroyed, the sample given and any related material and information.

A police officer may, before the end of a period referred to in subsection (3)(b) or (3)(c), apply, without notice to any other person, to the Magistrates' Court for an order extending that period and, if the court makes such an order, the reference to the period in subsection (3)(b) or (3)(c) is a reference to that period as so extended.

history.raw: S. 464ZGE(6) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: If the Magistrates' Court makes an order under subsection (6), it must give reasons for its decision and cause a copy of the order to be served on the person who voluntarily gave the sample.

If a sample or related material and information is destroyed in accordance with this section, the Chief Commissioner of Police must, within 14 days, give notice of the destruction to the person who voluntarily gave the sample.
A person who knowingly—
fails to destroy; or
uses, or causes or permits to be used—

a sample or related material and information required by this section to be destroyed is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

A person who at any time uses, or causes or permits to be used, or otherwise disseminates information derived from any sample or related material and information required by this section to be destroyed except in good faith for the purposes of section 464ZFD(2) is guilty of a summary offence punishable on conviction by level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).
This section does not prevent a police officer, in respect of a person who has voluntarily given a sample under sections 464ZGB to 464ZGD—

history.raw: S. 464ZGE(11) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: requesting, under section 464R, the person to undergo a forensic procedure; or
requesting, under section 464SC, the person to give a DNA profile sample; or
making an authorisation under section 464SE for the taking of a DNA profile sample from the person; or
making an application under section 464T or 464V for a court order directing the person to undergo a compulsory procedure.

nodes.heading: Application to court where consent to retention of sample withdrawn

history.raw: S. 464ZGF (1)(b) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: A police officer may apply to the Magistrates' Court for an order to retain a sample that has been voluntarily given by a person in accordance with sections 464ZGB to 464ZGD, and any related material and information, and the court may make an order accordingly, if during an investigation into the commission of an indictable offence—

history.raw: S. 464ZGF(1) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).
S. 464ZGF(1) (a)(ii) amended by No. 37/2014 s. 10(Sch. item 36.37).

nodes.text: either—
material reasonably believed to be from the body of a person who committed the indictable offence has been found—
at the scene of the offence; or
on the victim of the offence or on anything reasonably believed to have been worn or carried by the victim when the offence was committed; or
on an object or person reasonably believed to have been associated with the commission of the offence; or

if the offence is an offence against a provision of Subdivision (8A), (8B) or (8C) of Division 1 of Part I, and a police officer reasonably believes that a child has been conceived as a result of the commission of the offence and a sample has been taken from that child; and

a police officer reasonably believes that information obtained from the analysis of the sample voluntarily given by the person, and from any related material and information, has probative value in relation to the indictable offence being investigated; and
the person who voluntarily gave that sample has withdrawn his or her consent to the retention of that sample; and
the information obtained from the analysis of the voluntary sample, and from any related material and information, has not been destroyed in accordance with section 464ZGE(2)(a) and (3)(a).
A court hearing an application under subsection (1) must—
be satisfied on the balance of probabilities that there are reasonable grounds to believe that the person has committed the offence in respect of which the application is made; and
be satisfied that, in all the circumstances, the making of the order is justified.
If the court makes an order under subsection (1), it must give reasons for its decision and cause a copy of the order and reasons to be served on the person who voluntarily gave the sample.
A failure of a court to comply with subsection (3) does not invalidate any order made by it but constitutes non-compliance for the purposes of section 464ZE(1)(a).

nodes.heading: Voluntary samples given by police or VIFM personnel

nodes.text: In this section—

nodes.heading: Institute
nodes.text: means the Victorian Institute of Forensic Medicine established under the Victorian Institute of Forensic Medicine Act 2024;

history.raw: S. 464ZGFA(1) def. of Institute amended by No. 34/2024 s. 50(1).

nodes.heading: relevant agency
nodes.text: means—
Victoria Police; or
the Institute.
Any of the following persons may volunteer to give to a relevant agency a sample of material from which a DNA profile may be derived—
a member of Victoria Police personnel;
the Chief Executive Officer of the Institute or a person employed under section 30 or 31 of the Victorian Institute of Forensic Medicine Act 2024;
a visitor to—
any premises at which the Victoria Police Forensic Services Department performs functions; or
any premises at which the Institute performs any of its functions.
A sample may only be given under this section if the relevant agency has provided to the person volunteering to give the sample—

a written statement that the sample is to be provided for the purpose of comparing a DNA profile obtained from the sample against any other DNA profile held by the relevant agency to eliminate the person as a possible source of DNA in—
the investigation of a crime; or
the investigation of a reportable death within the meaning of the Coroners Act 2008; or
in the case of the Institute, testing conducted by the Institute in the performance of its objects and functions; and
a written statement of the requirements of section 464ZGFB(3) and (5).
A sample given under this section may be used only for the purpose referred to in subsection (3)(a).

Evidence of a sample given by a person under this section and any DNA profile obtained from the sample is inadmissible as evidence against the person, unless the person consents to the admission of the evidence, in—
any proceeding, whether civil or criminal; or
a proceeding arising out of, or connected with, an investigation under Division 6 of Part 4, Part 5, Part 7, Part 9 or Part 10 of the Victoria Police Act 2013 in respect of the person; or
a proceeding arising out of, or connected with, a critical incident (within the meaning of section 82 of the Victoria Police Act 2013).
In subsection (5) a proceeding includes a coronial inquest or inquiry.

A sample given under this section and any DNA profile obtained from the sample may not be released to any person outside the relevant agency unless the person who gave the sample consents to the release.

A person must not knowingly use, or cause or permit to be used, or otherwise disseminate information derived from, a sample given under this section, any DNA profile obtained from the sample or any related information, other than in accordance with this section.
Penalty: level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum).
An offence against subsection (8) is a summary offence.
This section does not affect any other power to require a person referred to in subsection (2) to provide a sample or to undergo a forensic procedure.

nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police is responsible for ensuring the destruction under this section of samples and DNA profiles that are held or managed by Victoria Police.
The Chief Executive Officer of the Institute is responsible for ensuring the destruction under this section of samples and DNA profiles that are held or managed by the Institute.
A DNA profile derived from a sample given under section 464ZGFA must be stored on a database that—
is not a DNA database; and
is not connected to any other database on which matching of DNA profiles occurs.
DNA database is defined in section 464(2).
A sample given under section 464ZGFA must not be entered in NCIDD.
A sample given under section 464ZGFA and a DNA profile derived from the sample must be destroyed if—

in the case of a sample given by the Chief Commissioner of Police, the Chief Commissioner requests the destruction of the sample by notice in writing to the Minister administering the Victoria Police Act 2013; or

in the case of a sample given by any other member of Victoria Police personnel or a visitor to any premises at which the Victoria Police Forensic Services Department performs functions, the member or visitor requests the destruction of the sample by notice in writing to the Chief Commissioner of Police; or
in the case of a sample given by the Chief Executive Officer of the Institute, the Chief Executive Officer requests the destruction of the sample by notice in writing to the Attorney-General; or

in the case of a sample given by an employee of the Institute or a visitor to any premises at which the Institute performs any of its functions, the employee or visitor requests the destruction of the sample by notice in writing to the Chief Executive Officer of the Institute; or

12 months have elapsed since the person who gave the sample ceased to be a member of Victoria Police personnel, the Chief Executive Officer of the Institute or an employee of the Institute, as the case may be.

Without affecting any other arrangements for destruction of samples, this section also applies, on and from its commencement, to a sample given voluntarily by a person referred to in section 464ZGFA(2) before the commencement of this section.
A person must not knowingly—
fail to destroy; or
use, or cause or permit to be used, or otherwise disseminate information derived from—
a sample, or a DNA profile derived from a sample, that is required by this section to be destroyed.
Penalty: level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum).

nodes.text: This section applies despite anything to the contrary in this Subdivision.
Subject to subsection (3), within 12 months of the commencement of Part 1.2 of the Youth Justice Act 2024, the Chief Commissioner of Police must destroy or cause to be destroyed—
any fingerprint taken from a person under this Subdivision in respect of the commission or alleged commission of an offence by the person when the person was under 12 years of age; and
any record, copy or photograph of that fingerprint.

The Chief Commissioner of Police is not required to destroy or cause to be destroyed a person's fingerprint referred to in subsection (2)(a) or a record, copy or photograph of that fingerprint if the person has died.

If a person's fingerprint and any record, copy or photograph of that fingerprint is required by this section to be destroyed, the Chief Commissioner of Police, on the request of that person, must notify the person in writing as to whether that fingerprint and other information has been destroyed.
Notice under subsection (4) must be given within 14 days after the Chief Commissioner of Police receives the person's request.
A person must not knowingly fail to destroy a fingerprint, or record, copy or photograph of a fingerprint, that is required by this section to be destroyed.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

A person must not knowingly use, or cause or permit to be used, or otherwise disseminate information derived from a fingerprint, or record, copy or photograph of a fingerprint, that is required by this section to be destroyed.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).
An offence against subsection (6) or (7) is a summary offence.

physically destroy; and

nodes.text: This section applies despite anything to the contrary in this Subdivision.

Subject to section 464ZFD(2), within 12 months of the commencement of Part 1.2 of the Youth Justice Act 2024, the Chief Commissioner of Police must destroy or cause to be destroyed any of the following taken from a person under this Subdivision in respect of the commission or alleged commission of an offence by the person when the person was under 12 years of age—
any sample taken from the person in a forensic procedure and any related material and information;
any DNA profile sample taken from the person and any related material and information;
any other sample taken from the person and any related material and information.

If a person's sample and any related material and information is required by this section to be destroyed, the Chief Commissioner of Police, on the request of that person, must notify the person in writing as to whether that sample and related material and information has been destroyed.
Notice under subsection (3) must be given within 14 days after the Chief Commissioner of Police receives the person's request.
A person must not knowingly fail to destroy a sample or any related material and information that is required by this section to be destroyed.
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

A person must not knowingly use, or cause or permit to be used, or otherwise disseminate information derived from a sample or any related material and information that is required by this section to be destroyed, except in good faith for the purposes of section 464ZFD(2).
Penalty: Level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).
An offence against subsection (5) or (6) is a summary offence.

if the information is derived from forensic material taken from a volunteer—the period after the information is placed on the DNA database that is agreed by the Chief Commissioner of Police and the volunteer;

A person who intentionally or recklessly causes any identifying information to be recorded or retained in a DNA database at any time after this Subdivision requires the forensic material to be destroyed is guilty of a summary offence and liable to level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

A responsible person who does not ensure that any identifying information on the volunteers (unlimited purposes) index or volunteers (limited purposes) index of the DNA database is removed from the database as soon as practicable after the end of the identifying period for the information is guilty of a summary offence and liable to level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

A responsible person who does not ensure that any identifying information relating to an offender on the serious offenders index of the DNA database is removed from the database as soon as practicable after becoming aware that the offender has been pardoned or acquitted of the offence concerned or if the conviction has been set aside is guilty of a summary offence and liable to level 8 imprisonment (1 year maximum) or a level 8 fine (120 penalty units maximum).

nodes.heading: Victorian information

nodes.heading: Inter-jurisdictional enforcement
nodes.text: Inter-jurisdictional enforcement

The Minister may enter into arrangements with the responsible Ministers of the participating jurisdictions for the establishment and maintenance, in one or more of those jurisdictions, of a register of orders for the carrying out of forensic procedures made under this Subdivision or corresponding laws of participating jurisdictions.

An order is registered when a copy of the order (being a copy certified as required under subsection (2A)) is registered in accordance with the law of the participating jurisdiction in which the register is kept.
The copy of the order must be certified by—
the person who made it; or
if that person is not available, a judicial officer of the participating jurisdiction in which the order was made.
An application for registration of an order, or for cancellation of registration of an order, may be made by an appropriate authority.

A person is authorised to carry out the forensic procedure authorised by an order that is registered in accordance with an arrangement referred to in section 464ZGL(1) anywhere in Victoria. The person is authorised to carry out the procedure in accordance with sections 464Y, 464Z and 464ZA and not otherwise.

A police officer, or other person assisting a police officer in accordance with this Subdivision or a corresponding law of a participating jurisdiction, is not compelled by this Subdivision, or an arrangement referred to in section 464ZGL(1), to execute an order registered under such an arrangement.
